recipes.recipe_name: Baked Pike-Perch and Potato Gratin with Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, golden-brown baked pike-perch and potato gratin rests on a simple, round ceramic plate. The gratin features tender, thin-sliced potatoes layered beneath flaky, cooked pike-perch chunks, with a slight golden crust on top. Beside it, a generous portion of vibrant orange-red tomato rice, cooked al dente, displays individual grains and specks of red from the tomato. A scattering of fresh, chopped green dill or parsley garnishes both the gratin and the rice. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually placed cloth napkin and a standard fork and knife. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the homely, inviting textures and colors of the meal. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a modest, satisfying single portion.

ingredients.name: Pike-perch fillets, skin on or off

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Lightly grease a medium baking dish (approx. 20x30 cm).
Slice potatoes thinly, about 3 mm thick. Pat dry with paper towels.
Season pike-perch fillets with salt and pepper.
Arrange half of the sliced potatoes in an even layer in the prepared baking dish.
Place pike-perch fillets over the potato layer. Top with remaining potato slices.
Whisk single cream with 100 ml of vegetable broth, salt, and pepper. Pour evenly over the potatoes and fish.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and fish is cooked through (75°C internal temperature). The top should be golden brown.
While the gratin bakes, prepare the tomato rice. Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the rice until well coated. Pour in the crushed tomatoes and remaining 500 ml vegetable broth.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-18 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff the tomato rice with a fork. Stir in half of the chopped dill or parsley.
Remove gratin from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Serve portions of baked pike-perch and potato gratin alongside the tomato rice. Garnish with remaining fresh dill or parsley.
notes: This recipe focuses on simple, comforting flavors and straightforward preparation, ideal for a hearty home-cooked meal.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Bell Pepper & Chickpea Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Bell Pepper & Chickpea Pasta is presented in a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic bowl on a light reclaimed wood table. The pasta, such as fusilli, is coated in a vibrant, rustic orange-red sauce. Interspersed are bright yellow and red diced bell pepper pieces, offering color and textural contrast. Cooked chickpeas are visible, adding an earthy tone and hearty substance. A generous sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped green parsley provides a natural, verdant garnish. A few toasted bell pepper seeds are scattered on top. Plating is minimalistic, with ample white space, highlighting the pasta's organic form and natural textures. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige rests beside the bowl, completing the eco-conscious setting.

ingredients.name: fresh bell peppers (one red, one yellow), diced
vegetable broth (ideally made from bell pepper trimmings/cores)
fresh parsley or basil, roughly chopped, for garnish
toasted bell pepper seeds (from the fresh bell peppers), for garnish

instructions: Prepare bell pepper broth: Simmer bell pepper cores, seeds (if not toasting), and any trimmings from the fresh bell peppers in 250 ml water for 15 minutes. Strain and reserve 100 ml broth. Discard solids.
Cook pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 150 ml pasta cooking water before draining.
Sauté aromatics: While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Build sauce: Add diced fresh bell peppers to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender-crisp. Stir in fermented bell pepper paste and the reserved 100 ml bell pepper broth. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Combine: Add drained chickpeas and nutritional yeast to the sauce. Stir well. Add the cooked pasta to the pan. Toss to coat evenly. Add reserved pasta cooking water gradually, 50 ml at a time, until the sauce reaches desired consistency.
Finish: Remove from heat. Stir in lemon juice, salt, and black pepper. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Plate: Serve immediately in shallow bowls. Garnish with fresh parsley or basil and toasted bell pepper seeds, if using.
notes: For the fermented bell pepper paste, store-bought fermented red pepper spread (like lacto-fermented pepper paste) works well. Alternatively, lacto-ferment red bell peppers at home for 5-7 days, then blend into a paste.
This recipe prioritizes using bell pepper trimmings to create a flavorful broth, minimizing food waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Tomato Rigatoni Starter
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Chicken and Tomato Rigatoni is presented in a shallow, clean white porcelain bowl. A small, neat mound of al dente rigatoni, tossed in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce, occupies the center. Tender, golden-brown 1.5 cm diced chicken pieces are evenly distributed throughout the pasta and sauce. A light dusting of freshly grated white Parmesan cheese covers the top, creating a delicate contrast. A few vibrant green, torn fresh basil leaves are scattered over the cheese, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish is placed on a simple wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro. A standard silver fork rests beside the bowl on a white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, with a soft, unobtrusive background that maintains a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 1.5 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes.
Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Add finely diced onion.
Sauté onion over medium heat for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, do not brown.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer sauce for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
While sauce simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Add cooked chicken and drained rigatoni to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Portion the pasta into four individual starter bowls.
Garnish each serving with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and torn fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Gnocchi with Salami and Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a single generous portion in a rustic, deep white ceramic baking dish. Golden-brown baked gnocchi, tender and plump, are coated in a vibrant, rich red tomato sauce. Irregularly diced salami pieces, some with slightly crisped edges, are scattered throughout the gnocchi, providing savory depth. Melted mozzarella, forming a bubbly, golden-brown crust on top, stretches appealingly. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are artfully torn and scattered over the bubbling cheese, offering a pop of color and freshness. The textures are a comforting blend of soft gnocchi, savory salami, and gooey cheese. The salami is diced into small cubes, and the mozzarella into small chunks. The dish rests on a simple wooden table, with a crisp white linen napkin to the side, under natural, even lighting, evoking a casual Italian trattoria.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with crusty Italian bread (pane di casa) to soak up the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Lightly grease a large baking dish.
Dice the onion into small pieces. Mince the garlic. Dice the salami into small cubes. Dice the mozzarella into small chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced salami to the skillet. Cook until slightly crispy, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring sauce to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook gnocchi according to package directions in a large pot of salted boiling water. Drain when gnocchi float to the surface.
Add cooked gnocchi to the tomato sauce. Add most of the diced mozzarella and half of the fresh basil, torn. Stir gently to combine.
Transfer gnocchi mixture to the prepared baking dish. Top with remaining mozzarella and grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Remove from oven. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves, torn.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Bean Chili
recipes.visual_description: A generous, steaming portion of hearty beef and bean chili is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, its rich reddish-brown hue inviting and warm. The ground beef is cooked to a fine crumble, mixed with diced tomatoes and plump, whole kidney beans, creating a satisfyingly thick and textured stew. A small dollop of creamy white sour cream sits gently on top, melting slightly into the chili, and a light sprinkling of vibrant green chopped cilantro adds a fresh pop of color. The bowl is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, with natural light casting a soft glow. A simple, sturdy metal spoon rests beside the bowl, and a casually folded cloth napkin adds to the homely, lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal, hinting at a cozy family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm cornbread.
Offer a side of tortilla chips for dipping.
Accompany with steamed white rice.

ingredients.name: Canned Kidney Beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef. Cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Stir well.
Add drained and rinsed kidney beans. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for at least 30-45 minutes, stirring occasionally. For deeper flavor, simmer longer.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with a dollop of sour cream and fresh chopped cilantro, if desired.
notes: This chili can be made ahead of time. Flavors deepen overnight.
Adjust chili powder to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Garlic Chicken with Roasted Butternut Squash and Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan Garlic Chicken and Roasted Butternut Squash Pasta is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy pasta, rich with a light golden-beige sauce, is centrally mounded. Visible within the pasta are substantial, seared chicken chunks, approximately 3-4 cm in size, exhibiting a golden-brown crust. Interspersed throughout are soft, caramelized cubes of roasted butternut squash, their vibrant orange color providing a warm contrast. Fresh green spinach leaves are lightly wilted into the pasta, adding a pop of color and freshness. Nestled alongside the pasta, or slightly overlapping, are golden-brown, crispy roasted potato cubes, approximately 2 cm, some with visible flecks of fresh rosemary. A light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese covers the dish, and a few fresh parsley leaves serve as a simple, fresh garnish. The plate rests on a light, natural wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the textures. The background is a softly blurred, modern bistro setting, suggesting a casual yet refined dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a lemon vinaigrette.
Pair with a light Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio or a Chianti.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Maris Piper or Yukon Gold)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Prepare vegetables. Peel and cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Peel and cut butternut squash into 2 cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Roast potatoes. Toss potato cubes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and rosemary sprigs. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until golden and tender.
Roast squash. Toss butternut squash cubes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and thyme sprigs. Spread on a separate baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized.
Cook pasta. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Prepare chicken. Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Sear chicken. Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken pieces. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Reduce heat. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C (approximately 8-10 minutes total). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Make sauce. Add minced garlic to the same pan. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits. Stir in cream. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Combine. Add cooked pasta, roasted butternut squash, and cooked chicken chunks to the pan with the sauce. Add spinach. Toss to combine until spinach wilts. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese. If needed, add reserved pasta water to achieve desired consistency.
Serve. Serve immediately, topping each portion with the roasted rosemary potatoes. Garnish with fresh parsley or extra Parmesan.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked thoroughly to 75°C internal temperature.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing chicken or roasting vegetables to ensure proper browning and crispiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef & Mushroom Salisbury Steaks
recipes.visual_description: A single, robust, oval-shaped beef patty, seared to a rich brown crust, rests centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The patty is generously coated and surrounded by a glossy, dark brown mushroom and onion gravy. The gravy contains distinct, tender slices of sautéed cremini mushrooms and caramelized yellow onion pieces. A vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley provides a fresh, contrasting garnish atop the patty and gravy. The dish is presented with moderate negative space, highlighting the substantial portion. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, standard silver flatware, and a folded cotton napkin positioned beside the plate, all under soft, natural, even lighting with a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with creamy mashed potatoes.
Serve alongside steamed green beans or buttered corn.
Offer a simple side salad with a vinaigrette.
instructions: Dice 100g of yellow onion finely. Mince garlic.
In a large bowl, combine ground beef, diced onion, minced garlic, panko breadcrumbs, egg, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form the mixture into four oval-shaped patties, about 2 cm thick.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add patties to the skillet. Sear 4-5 minutes per side until deeply browned. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove patties from skillet and set aside.

Slice remaining 150g yellow onion thinly. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and 30g butter to the same skillet. Add sliced onions and sliced mushrooms. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Sprinkle 30g flour over the onions and mushrooms. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in 500 ml beef broth and 15 ml Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until gravy thickens. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Return cooked patties to the skillet with the gravy. Simmer 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Ensure patties are fully coated in gravy.
Garnish generously with chopped fresh parsley before serving.
notes: For best results, use ground beef with 80/20 or 85/15 fat content for flavor and moisture.
Do not overmix the ground beef mixture to ensure tender patties.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemongrass Chicken Dumplings
recipes.visual_description: Four to five golden-brown pan-fried and steamed dumplings are arranged neatly on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The dumplings have visible pleats and a slight crispness on their flat bottoms. They are arranged in a slight curve or small cluster, allowing for negative space. A small, fresh sprig of coriander or a sprinkle of finely chopped chives rests gently on top of the dumplings. A small, white ceramic dipping bowl filled with the light brown soy-based sauce is placed beside the dumplings. The dumplings are a warm golden-brown with hints of light green from the herbs inside. The dipping sauce is a rich amber-brown. The white plate provides a clean contrast. The dumplings show crisp exteriors and a plump, soft interior. The sauce is fluid. Ingredients within the dumpling are finely minced or diced. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A grey cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting from the side, creating soft shadows. The background is a blurred, casual restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chili oil or a spicy sriracha sauce for extra heat.
Enjoy as a shared appetizer.
Accompany with other small plates.
instructions: Prepare dumpling filling. Combine chicken mince, minced lemongrass, chopped coriander, diced onion, minced garlic, grated nutmeg, black pepper, soy sauce, sesame oil, and cornstarch in a large bowl. Mix well until combined.
Assemble dumplings. Place 1 teaspoon of filling in the center of a dumpling wrapper. Moisten the edges with water. Fold wrapper in half to form a half-moon. Pleat the edges to seal.
Repeat for remaining filling and wrappers.
Cook dumplings. Heat 1 tbsp neutral oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Place dumplings in a single layer, flat side down. Cook 2-3 minutes until bottoms are golden brown.
Add 125 ml water to the pan. Immediately cover with a lid. Steam 8-10 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature. Water should evaporate.
Remove lid. Cook 1-2 minutes more if needed to crisp bottoms.
Prepare dipping sauce. Combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, chopped chives, minced garlic, and chili flakes (if using) in a small bowl. Mix well.
Serve dumplings hot with dipping sauce.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked thoroughly to 75°C (167°F).
Do not overcrowd the pan when cooking dumplings. Cook in batches if necessary.
traditional_techniques: Finely mincing ingredients for filling consistency

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken Skewers
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown chicken cubes, seared to perfection, are threaded onto small wooden skewers. Six skewers are artfully arranged on a clean, rectangular white porcelain platter, slightly angled to create visual interest. Each chicken cube exhibits a beautiful char on its edges, showcasing the grilling technique. A vibrant sprinkle of finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley garnishes the skewers, adding a pop of green and aromatic freshness. Bright yellow lemon wedges are strategically placed on the platter, ready for a squeeze. The presentation is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The platter rests on a simple light wooden table, alongside a small white ceramic bowl holding a creamy, pale tahini dipping sauce. A folded white cotton napkin lies nearby. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting its appealing textures and colors, creating an inviting, sophisticated snack presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of a mezze platter with pita bread and fresh salads.
Offer small bowls of pickles or olives on the side.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2.5 cm uniform cubes.
Combine olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl. Whisk well.
Add chicken cubes to the marinade. Toss to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, up to 4 hours.
Soak wooden skewers in water for 20 minutes to prevent burning.
Thread chicken cubes onto skewers. Do not overcrowd.
Preheat a grill pan or outdoor grill to medium-high heat.
Grill skewers for 3-4 minutes per side until chicken is golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
For the tahini sauce: Whisk tahini, 30 ml lemon juice, and cold water in a small bowl until smooth and creamy. Add more water if needed for desired consistency. Season with a pinch of salt.
Arrange cooked skewers on a serving platter. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon wedges. Serve immediately with tahini sauce.
notes: Ensure all ingredients used are certified kosher.
The tahini sauce is parve, making the dish suitable for a kosher meal.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom & Sauerkraut Savory Bites
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve individual savory bites are artfully arranged on a light, natural-textured platter, such as reclaimed wood or a beige ceramic slab. Each canapé features a small, blanched cabbage leaf, gently cupped, serving as a natural, edible vessel. Inside, a generous spoon of earthy, finely pulsed mushroom and sauerkraut filling, its rich brown and green tones visible. The filling is crowned with a delicate dollop of pale, creamy horseradish-tarragon sauce, offering a stark, clean contrast. A single, fresh tarragon sprig garnishes each bite. The presentation is minimalistic, highlighting the natural forms and colors of the ingredients. The setting features a light, undyed linen napkin and soft, natural light, reflecting sustainable and rustic Russian culinary traditions.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of a traditional Russian zakuski (appetizer) spread
Pair with chilled vodka or kvass
instructions: Gently remove 8-12 large outer leaves from cabbage. Blanch in boiling salted water for 1-2 minutes until pliable. Drain. Pat dry. Trim into desired cup shapes, approximately 8-10 cm diameter. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add finely diced mushrooms. Cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 8-10 minutes.

Add drained, finely chopped sauerkraut to the mushroom mixture. Stir well. Pour in vegetable broth. Simmer for 5 minutes until liquid reduces. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
Transfer the mushroom-sauerkraut mixture to a food processor. Pulse briefly until a coarse, spreadable mixture forms. Do not over-process; retain some texture.
In a small bowl, combine plant-based yogurt, grated horseradish, half of the chopped tarragon, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Mix until smooth.
Place each blanched cabbage cup on a serving platter. Spoon 1-2 tablespoons of the mushroom-sauerkraut filling into each cabbage cup. Top each with a small dollop of the horseradish-tarragon cream.
Garnish with a small tarragon sprig. Refrigerate for 15 minutes before serving for flavors to meld.
notes: Use outer cabbage leaves for the cups to promote a zero-waste approach.

recipes.recipe_name: Vegetarian Golubtsy (Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
recipes.visual_description: Two generous vegetarian golubtsy, or stuffed cabbage rolls, are neatly arranged on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. Each roll, encased in tender blanched cabbage, reveals a hearty filling of finely diced mushrooms, grated potato, and cooked pearl barley. A rich, deep red tomato-based sauce, infused with sautéed onions and carrots, is generously spooned over the rolls. A dollop of creamy white smetana sits atop one golubets, contrasting beautifully with the vibrant sauce. Fresh green dill sprigs are artfully placed for garnish. The dish is presented on a rustic wooden table, accompanied by a small side bowl of smetana, a traditional silver spoon, and a simple linen napkin. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the textures and colors, highlighting the comforting, authentic Russian presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a generous dollop of smetana (sour cream).
Garnish with fresh chopped dill.
Traditionally served with black bread on the side.
instructions: Remove core from cabbage head. Blanch cabbage in a large pot of boiling salted water for 10-15 minutes. Leaves should soften. Carefully peel off individual leaves. Trim thick veins from leaves.
Cook pearl barley according to package instructions until tender. Drain well.
Dice one onion finely. Slice mushrooms. Grate potatoes. Grate carrot. Mince garlic.

Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large pan. Sauté diced onion until translucent. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until softened and moisture evaporates. Add grated potatoes and minced garlic. Cook for 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Combine sautéed vegetables with cooked barley in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper. This is your filling.
Lay a cabbage leaf flat. Place a spoonful of filling near the stem end. Fold sides over filling. Roll tightly from bottom to top to form a compact parcel. Repeat with remaining leaves and filling.
Heat remaining 15 ml vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven. Sauté the second diced onion and grated carrot until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, and bay leaf to the pot. Bring sauce to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Carefully arrange stuffed cabbage rolls in a single layer in the simmering sauce. Ensure rolls are mostly submerged. Add more broth or water if needed.
Cover pot. Simmer on low heat for 45-60 minutes, or until cabbage is very tender and filling is heated through.
Serve hot. Garnish each serving with a generous dollop of sour cream and fresh chopped dill.
notes: This vegetarian version of Golubtsy offers a hearty and satisfying main course.
The use of pearl barley and mushrooms provides a rich, earthy texture and flavor that complements the tender cabbage.
traditional_techniques: Slow simmering in a flavorful sauce

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Lentil Pot
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Hearty Beef and Lentil Pot is presented in a clean, wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The stew is rich, deep brown, showcasing tender, irregular chunks of beef nestled among vibrant red lentils, glossy black beans, and distinct pieces of diced red and green bell peppers. The texture is hearty yet refined, with visible separation of ingredients. A generous scattering of fresh chopped parsley provides a bright green contrast on top. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded off-white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and texture. The background is a soft, blurred restaurant setting, minimal and unobtrusive, allowing the dish to be the focal point.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, trimmed, cut into 3 cm cubes
Canned black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef cubes in batches until well browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced red and green bell peppers. Cook for another 5 minutes until slightly tender.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef stock, rinsed red lentils, dried thyme, and bay leaf. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Stir in rinsed black beans. Continue to simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, allowing the stew to thicken slightly and flavors to meld.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle the Hearty Beef and Lentil Pot into individual serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Dark Beer and Chili Bean Soup
recipes.visual_description: A deep, inviting ceramic bowl holds a generous portion of Rustic Dark Beer and Chili Bean Soup. The soup is a rich, earthy reddish-brown, reflecting the dark beer, tomatoes, and chili. Visible tender, diced onions and plump, softened kidney beans are suspended in the slightly thick, comforting broth. The surface is subtly textured, with a scattering of vibrant green, chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley adding a pop of color. A thick, rustic slice of crusty, golden-brown bread rests casually beside the bowl, ready for dipping. The setting is a well-worn wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, natural light, conveying a cozy, homely atmosphere. A simple, sturdy metal spoon and a casually folded cloth napkin complete the unpretentious, inviting scene.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika, and ground cumin. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Stir in canned diced tomatoes, dark beer, and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Add drained and rinsed kidney beans. Continue to simmer for another 5 minutes, heating beans through.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately with thick slices of crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Blini with Spiced Avocado Spread
recipes.special_requests: vegetarian, yummy, Russian, everyday cooking cuisine
recipes.visual_description: Plating: 8-12 small, golden-brown potato blini, each about 5cm diameter. Blini are arranged casually on a traditional Russian wooden serving board or a simple ceramic platter. Each blini is topped with a generous dollop of creamy, pale green avocado spread. The spread has flecks of red chili and a dusting of vibrant red paprika. Fresh green dill sprigs are placed on top of each canapé. The blini show slightly irregular, homemade edges. Setting: The platter sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden kitchen table. A simple, slightly wrinkled linen napkin in a neutral color is casually placed nearby. Lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen. The background is slightly out of focus, showing glimpses of a lived-in family kitchen, perhaps a traditional Russian tea kettle or ceramic ware. The overall impression is one of rustic, comforting, and authentic home cooking.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with strong black tea or kvass.
Offer small bowls of sour cream or gherkins on the side, in traditional zakuski style.
instructions: Peel and boil potatoes until very tender. Drain well. Mash thoroughly until smooth.
In a large bowl, combine mashed potatoes, flour, milk, egg, baking powder, salt, and pepper. Mix until a smooth batter forms.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Spoon tablespoonfuls of batter into the hot pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Transfer blini to a wire rack to cool.
For the spread, halve and pit avocados. Scoop flesh into a bowl. Mash with a fork.
Finely mince garlic clove and red chili. Add to mashed avocado.
Stir in smoked paprika, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Mix well until combined.
To assemble, place a dollop of spiced avocado spread on each potato blini. Garnish with a small sprig of fresh dill.
notes: This recipe creates a comforting, everyday Russian-style canapé.
The blini are more like small potato pancakes than thin crepes, fitting the home cooking style.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Potato and Poblano Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of thick, creamy, pale yellow potato soup fills a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The soup’s surface is rich and inviting, with visible small, soft potato chunks and flecks of finely diced green poblano. A dollop of cool, white sour cream rests off-center, gently swirling into the soup. Fresh, vibrant green dill sprigs are sprinkled over the sour cream and soup, adding a pop of color and freshness. Small, neatly diced cubes of ripe green avocado are scattered on top. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm wooden dining table. A casually folded linen napkin and a thick slice of dark rye bread are placed beside the bowl. The scene is lit with warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a comforting, lived-in atmosphere, characteristic of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of dark rye bread (Borodinsky bread is excellent).
Offer extra sour cream (smetana) at the table for guests to add as desired.
Accompany with pickled vegetables, such as cucumbers or cabbage, for a traditional Russian touch.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Place poblano chiles on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until skin is blistered and charred. Transfer chiles to a bowl. Cover tightly with plastic wrap. Let steam for 10 minutes.
Peel, deseed, and finely chop the roasted poblanos. Set aside.
Peel and dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Dice onion and carrot. Mince garlic.
In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add annatto seeds and cumin seeds. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Remove seeds if desired, or leave them for texture.
Add diced onion and carrot to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and chopped poblano. Cook for 2 minutes more.
Add diced potatoes and vegetable broth to the pot. Add thyme sprigs. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are very tender.

Remove thyme sprigs. Using an immersion blender, blend about half of the soup until creamy, leaving some potato chunks for texture. Alternatively, carefully transfer half of the soup to a regular blender and blend. Return blended portion to the pot.
Grate Chihuahua cheese. Add grated cheese to the soup. Stir until cheese is completely melted and soup is smooth and creamy. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Dice avocado just before serving.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish each serving with a dollop of sour cream, a sprinkle of fresh dill, and diced avocado.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Poblano & Avocado Tartines
recipes.special_requests: vegetarian, yummy, Only not Mexican food cuisine
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents individual, rustic flatbreads, each a warm, pale orange hue from the annatto, with flecks of dark green thyme baked into their soft, slightly blistered surface. A generous, creamy layer of vibrant green avocado and subtly textured fermented poblano spread is spooned onto each flatbread. The spread shows soft, mashed avocado interspersed with small, irregular pieces of the unique, pale green fermented poblano. A scattering of finely crumbled creamy white Chihuahua cheese rests atop the spread, providing a textural contrast. A few delicate fresh thyme sprigs are placed casually on each tartine. The tartines are arranged naturally on a large, light-colored, handcrafted ceramic platter or a reclaimed wood board, allowing ample negative space. The setting features a light bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin in beige, and soft natural lighting from the side, with a clean, minimalist background showing subtle plant elements. The composition is clean and ingredient-focused.
instructions: Prepare Flatbread Dough: In a bowl, combine warm water, yeast, and sugar. Let stand 5 minutes until foamy.
Add flour, annatto powder, 5g chopped fresh thyme, 5g salt, and 15ml olive oil. Mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead Dough: Turn dough onto a lightly floured surface. Knead 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
First Rise: Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl. Cover with a cloth. Let rise in a warm place 1 hour, or until doubled.
Shape Flatbreads: Punch down dough. Divide into 8 equal pieces. Roll each piece into an oval, about 5mm thick.
Cook Flatbreads: Heat a dry cast-iron pan or griddle over medium-high heat. Cook each flatbread 2-3 minutes per side, until puffed and lightly charred. Stack on a plate, cover to keep warm.
Prepare Poblano-Avocado Spread: In a bowl, mash avocados. Add chopped fermented poblano, ground cumin, remaining 5g chopped fresh thyme, lime juice, and a pinch of salt. Mix well. Do not overmix.
Assemble Tartines: Spread a generous amount of poblano-avocado mixture onto each warm flatbread.
Garnish: Crumble Chihuahua cheese over the spread. Drizzle with a little olive oil. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Poblano and Avocado Quesadillas
recipes.visual_description: The quesadillas are golden brown, with a slightly crisp exterior. They are cut into irregular wedges, revealing a warm, creamy interior. Inside, pockets of melted, vibrant orange-hued chihuahua cheese mingle with soft, pale green mashed avocado. Darker green, smoky diced poblano pieces and translucent onion flecks are visible throughout the filling. The quesadillas are casually piled on a rustic ceramic serving plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A small bowl of vibrant green chopped cilantro is positioned nearby for garnish. Fresh lime wedges are scattered around the plate, adding a bright color contrast. Warm, cozy light illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and inviting colors of the snack.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of salsa verde or pico de gallo.
Offer extra lime wedges for squeezing.
Present on a large, communal platter for sharing.
instructions: Roast poblano chiles. Place on a baking sheet. Broil until skin is blistered and charred, about 5-7 minutes per side.
Transfer roasted chiles to a bowl. Cover tightly with plastic wrap. Let steam for 10 minutes.
Peel, seed, and dice roasted poblanos into small cubes.
In a small bowl, combine shredded chihuahua cheese with annatto powder. Mix well.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced poblano. Cook for 2 minutes. Stir in ground cumin. Remove from heat.
Halve and pit avocados. Scoop out flesh. Lightly mash with a fork. Season with salt.
Warm tortillas in a dry pan.
Lay a warm tortilla flat. Spread a thin layer of mashed avocado on one half.
Spoon some poblano-onion mixture over avocado.
Sprinkle generously with annatto-spiced chihuahua cheese.
Fold the other half of the tortilla over to create a half-moon.
Cook quesadilla in a dry or lightly oiled pan over medium heat. Cook until cheese is melted and tortilla is golden brown and crisp, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Repeat for remaining quesadillas.
Cut each quesadilla into 2-3 wedges.
Serve immediately with fresh cilantro and lime wedges.
traditional_techniques: Roasting chiles for charring and steaming to remove skin

recipes.recipe_name: Honey Financiers with Sweet Wine Gel
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform miniature financiers are elegantly arranged on a pristine white Carrara marble serving platter. Each financier, a golden-brown rectangle with subtly crisp edges, is coated in a delicate, translucent honey glaze that reflects the light. A precisely placed, vibrant dollop of clear, shimmering sweet wine gel rests atop each financier, providing a striking contrast in color and texture. The composition is minimalist and organic, with ample negative space enhancing the architectural precision of each petit four. The presentation is elevated by the luxurious marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and dramatic professional lighting that casts subtle, artistic shadows, emphasizing the refined simplicity and flawless execution.

ingredients.name: Sweet white wine (e.g., Sauternes, Ice Wine)

instructions: Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook until golden brown and nutty (beurre noisette). Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Let cool slightly.
In a separate bowl, whisk almond flour, all-purpose flour, powdered sugar, and salt.
Lightly whisk egg whites until just frothy. Do not whip to peaks.
Add 30g honey and egg whites to dry ingredients. Mix gently until just combined.
Gradually fold in the cooled brown butter until smooth. Do not overmix.
Cover batter and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, preferably overnight.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly butter and flour miniature financier molds.
Fill molds two-thirds full with batter.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until edges are golden brown and centers are set.
Remove from oven. Let cool in molds, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
For Sweet Wine Gel: In a small saucepan, whisk sweet wine and agar-agar. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour gel mixture into a shallow dish. Refrigerate until firm (at least 1 hour).
Once firm, cut gel into cubes. Transfer to a blender. Blend on high speed until completely smooth and fluid.
Pass gel through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
For Honey Glaze: Bloom gelatin powder in 10ml cold water.
Combine 50g honey and remaining 10ml water in a small saucepan. Heat gently until warm.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved.
Let glaze cool to lukewarm, about 30°C (86°F), before using. It should be thin but able to coat a spoon.
Place cooled financiers on a wire rack set over parchment paper.
Carefully spoon or brush a thin, even layer of honey glaze over each financier, allowing excess to drip off. Let glaze set slightly.
Just before serving, place a small, artful dollop of the sweet wine gel on top of each financier.
notes: For best results, prepare financier batter the day before.
Ensure sweet wine gel is completely smooth for a professional finish.
The honey glaze should be thin enough to coat without being thick or opaque.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Mexican Black Bean and Hominy Stew
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, deep terracotta ceramic bowl sits on a worn wooden dining table. The bowl is filled with a rich, dark brown black bean and hominy stew, its surface dotted with vibrant red tomato pieces and golden hominy. Steam gently rises. On top, generous chunks of bright green diced avocado are casually placed, alongside generous crumbles of white, salty Cotija cheese. Fresh, vibrant green cilantro leaves are scattered over the top. The stew has a thick, hearty texture. A simple, rough-textured linen napkin in a muted earth tone is casually draped beside the bowl. A traditional clay water pitcher and a stack of warm corn tortillas are in the soft-focused background. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for dipping.
Offer lime wedges on the side for a fresh squeeze.
Serve with a side of pickled jalapeños or a simple salsa roja.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin powder, and chili powder. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rinsed black beans, rinsed hominy, diced tomatoes, and vegetable broth.
Bring the stew to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle generous portions of hot stew into individual serving bowls.
Top each bowl with diced avocado and crumbled cotija cheese.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve immediately.
notes: For extra heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper with the chili powder.
This stew thickens as it cools; add a splash of broth when reheating if desired.
traditional_techniques: Sofrito (sautéing aromatics and spices as a base)

recipes.recipe_name: Financier de Porc Doux with Ginger-Apple Compote, Coconut Sorbet, and Almond Lace
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated dessert centered on a pristine white bone china plate. The focal point is a golden-brown, rectangular Financier de Porc Doux, its top a rich, caramelized hue. Beside it, a perfectly formed, smooth quenelle of creamy white Coconut Sorbet glistens. Adjacent, a small, artfully placed dollop of Ginger-Apple Compote, with visible diced apple and ginger flecks, offers a warm, amber tone. A delicate, golden Almond Lace Tuile, thin and crisp, stands vertically for height and texture. Abundant negative space emphasizes the minimalist, sophisticated composition. The setting is a premium white Carrara marble surface, with dramatic professional lighting creating subtle shadows. A perfectly folded white linen napkin is placed subtly to the side. The presentation is clean, precise, highlighting luxurious ingredients and masterful execution.
instructions: Prepare Financiers: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat until browned and nutty (brown butter). Strain through a fine sieve into a bowl. Add rendered pork fat to brown butter. Let cool slightly.
Whisk icing sugar, almond flour, and plain flour in a large bowl. Add egg whites. Whisk until smooth. Slowly whisk in brown butter and pork fat mixture until fully combined.
Cover batter. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour four financier molds. Fill molds two-thirds full with batter.
Bake 15-18 minutes, or until golden brown and edges are crisp. Cool on a wire rack.
Prepare Ginger-Apple Compote: Peel, core, and dice apples into 1 cm cubes. Peel and finely grate ginger.

Combine diced apples, grated ginger, cinnamon stick, granulated sugar, and lemon juice in a small saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat. Stir occasionally until apples are tender and liquid has reduced to a syrupy consistency, about 15-20 minutes. Remove cinnamon stick. Cool completely.
Prepare Coconut Sorbet: Combine coconut cream, granulated sugar, water, and salt in a saucepan. Heat gently, stirring until sugar dissolves. Do not boil. Chill mixture thoroughly.
Churn mixture in an ice cream maker according to manufacturer's instructions until frozen. Transfer to a freezer-safe container. Freeze until firm.
Prepare Almond Lace Tuiles: Whisk 20g icing sugar, 10g plain flour, and 1 egg white until smooth. Stir in 15g melted butter. Stir in flaked almonds.

Spread thin circles of batter onto a silicone mat or parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake at 160°C for 5-7 minutes, until golden and crisp. Immediately shape over a rolling pin or cylinder if desired for a curved shape. Cool completely.

Assembly: Place one financier on each plate. Form a quenelle of coconut sorbet next to the financier. Spoon a small amount of ginger-apple compote artfully beside the sorbet. Lean an almond lace tuile against the financier or sorbet for height.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Bean and Hominy Fritters with Avocado Crema
recipes.special_requests: vegetarian, This meal is simple, but very filling cuisine
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, inviting food photograph of Black Bean and Hominy Fritters presented as a starter. Three golden-brown, pan-fried fritters, approximately 5 cm in diameter with visible textures of black beans and hominy, are arranged slightly overlapping on a pristine white round porcelain plate. A smooth, pale green dollop of avocado crema artfully sits atop the fritters, with a few delicate streaks. White, crumbly Cotija cheese is scattered generously over the crema and around the fritters. Vibrant green, roughly chopped fresh cilantro leaves are sprinkled over the dish, providing a fresh contrast. The plate is positioned centrally on a simple light wooden table surface, capturing natural, even lighting that highlights the textures and colors. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere, allowing the dish to be the clear focal point. The fritters are whole, not sliced or fanned. All elements are well-proportioned, creating an appealing and professional presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of lime wedges for an extra burst of freshness.
Can be accompanied by a small dish of pickled red onions.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, rinsed and drained
Canned hominy corn, rinsed and drained

instructions: In a large bowl, combine rinsed black beans and hominy. Mash about half of the black beans and hominy with a fork or potato masher. Leave remaining beans and hominy whole for texture.
Add diced red onion, minced garlic, flour, cumin, smoked paprika, egg, salt, and pepper to the bowl. Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Form the mixture into 12 small patties, approximately 5 cm in diameter and 1.5 cm thick.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Carefully place fritters into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary.
Fry fritters for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crisp. Transfer cooked fritters to a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
For the avocado crema, scoop avocado flesh into a blender or food processor. Add lime juice, half of the chopped cilantro, and Mexican crema. Blend until smooth and creamy. Season with salt to taste.
To serve, arrange 3 fritters on each plate. Spoon a generous dollop of avocado crema over the fritters. Sprinkle with crumbled Cotija cheese and remaining fresh cilantro.
notes: Ensure black beans and hominy are well-drained to prevent soggy fritters.
For a spicier kick, add a pinch of cayenne pepper or a finely minced serrano chili to the fritter mixture.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Guacamole Dip
recipes.visual_description: A generous, unpretentious mound of chunky, vibrant green guacamole is centered in a rustic, shallow ceramic serving bowl. The guacamole shows natural variations in texture, with some avocado pieces still visible alongside finely diced red onion, bright green flecks of cilantro, and small pieces of shredded cheddar cheese peeking through. A light dusting of coarse salt crystals is visible on the surface. Around the guacamole, a casual, inviting arrangement of golden-brown tortilla chips is scattered on the same serving plate or platter, some leaning against the bowl, others flat. The chips have a slightly irregular, homemade appearance. The colors are natural and inviting: rich green from the avocado, hints of purple from the red onion, bright green from chili and cilantro, and warm yellow-orange from the cheese. The scene is set on a well-worn, light-colored wooden kitchen table, showing subtle signs of use. The serving bowl is an everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic piece in a neutral tone. A simple, textured cloth napkin in a complementary muted color is casually draped beside the bowl. The lighting is warm and soft, mimicking natural light from a kitchen window, casting gentle shadows that add depth without being harsh. The background is slightly blurred but suggests a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere, perhaps with a glimpse of a simple counter or a small, everyday utensil.
instructions: Halve avocados. Remove pits. Scoop flesh into a medium bowl.
Mash avocado with a fork until desired consistency. Leave some chunks.
Add finely diced red onion, finely minced green chili, and chopped cilantro.
Pour in lime juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Gently fold in shredded cheddar cheese. Mix until just combined.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Transfer guacamole to a serving bowl. Serve immediately with tortilla chips.

recipes.recipe_name: Sopa de Tortilla Vegetariana
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Sopa de Tortilla Vegetariana is presented in a deep, rustic, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. The rich, reddish-brown broth, made from simmered tomatoes and chipotle chiles, fills the bowl. Crispy, golden-brown corn tortilla strips, cut into thin batons, are partially submerged in the soup, some standing upright, offering a textural contrast. Fresh, vibrant green avocado slices or large cubes are arranged casually on top, their creamy texture visible. A scattering of bright green chopped cilantro and a fresh lime wedge complete the presentation, adding color and freshness. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden kitchen table, possibly with a simple, woven placemat. Natural, warm light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. The overall presentation is homely and comforting, emphasizing the simple, hearty nature of the dish with natural, unfussy arrangement.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lime wedges for individual preference.
Offer small bowls of crumbled queso fresco or a dollop of Mexican crema on the side.
Traditionally served as a hearty appetizer or a light meal.
instructions: Cut corn tortillas into thin strips (about 0.5 cm wide).

Heat 30 ml of vegetable oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium-high heat. Fry tortilla strips in batches until golden and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and place on a paper towel-lined plate to drain. Season lightly with salt.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 20 ml of oil to the pot. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chipotle chiles, adobo sauce, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften and flavors meld.
Carefully transfer the tomato mixture to a blender. Add 250 ml of vegetable broth. Blend until smooth. Be cautious when blending hot liquids.
Pour the blended mixture back into the pot. Add the remaining 1.25 litres of vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Season the soup with salt and pepper to taste. Simmer for 10-15 minutes to allow flavors to deepen.

To serve, ladle the hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish each bowl generously with crispy tortilla strips, sliced or diced avocado, fresh cilantro, and a lime wedge. If desired, add a dollop of Mexican crema or crumbled queso fresco.
notes: For extra crunch, you can bake the tortilla strips instead of frying them. Toss with a little oil and bake at 180°C until crispy.
Adjust the amount of chipotle chile to control the level of spice.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chickpea & Kale Bowl with Herbed Cottage Cheese
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a clean, shallow white porcelain bowl. Creamy, pale whipped herbed cottage cheese forms the base. Golden-brown roasted chickpeas, whole and split, are clustered on one side, offering crisp texture. Adjacent, dark green, roughly chopped sautéed kale forms a tender mound. Bright red cherry tomato halves and crisp small-diced cucumber pieces are arranged on the other side, with fine slivers of red onion, creating a fresh, colorful counterpoint. Fresh dill sprigs and a light dusting of red sumac powder garnish. A subtle olive oil sheen glistens. Professional, approachable plating features moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table, with a folded white cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting fresh ingredients.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss drained chickpeas with 30ml olive oil, cumin, paprika, 2g salt, and 2g black pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast chickpeas for 20-25 minutes, or until golden and slightly crispy. Shake sheet halfway through.

While chickpeas roast, prepare herbed cottage cheese. In a food processor, combine cottage cheese, half of the chopped dill, half of the chopped parsley, all of the chopped mint, zest of one lemon, 2g salt, and 2g black pepper. Process until smooth and creamy. Set aside.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add kale to the pan. Cook, stirring frequently, until wilted and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Set aside.

Prepare cucumber salad. In a medium bowl, combine diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, finely diced red onion, remaining 2 minced garlic cloves, juice of one lemon, and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Stir to combine.
To serve, spread a generous portion of whipped cottage cheese on the bottom of each shallow bowl.
Arrange roasted chickpeas and sautéed kale over the cottage cheese.
Top with a portion of the fresh cucumber salad.
Garnish with fresh dill sprigs, a sprinkle of sumac, and a final drizzle of olive oil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chunky Black Bean and Avocado Dip
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of chunky black bean and avocado dip sits in a rustic, light-colored ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The dip is a hearty mix of creamy mashed black beans, whole black beans, and vibrant green diced avocado. Flecks of finely diced red onion, minced garlic, and bright green chopped cilantro are visible throughout. A few minced red jalapeño pieces add subtle color. The dip is casually mounded in the bowl, creating a comforting, inviting texture. A pile of golden, crisp tortilla chips is arranged organically around the bowl, ready for dipping. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A simple, casually placed cloth napkin completes the homely scene, emphasizing a relaxed family meal.
instructions: Drain and rinse black beans thoroughly. Transfer half of the beans to a medium bowl. Mash these beans with a fork until mostly smooth, leaving some texture.
Mince the garlic cloves. Finely dice the red onion. Mince the jalapeño pepper, removing seeds for less heat if desired.
Halve, pit, and scoop the flesh from the ripe avocados. Dice the avocado flesh into small cubes.
Add the remaining whole black beans, diced avocado, minced red onion, minced garlic, and minced jalapeño to the bowl with the mashed beans.
Pour in the fresh lime juice. Add the ground cumin and a pinch of salt. Coarsely chop the fresh cilantro and add to the bowl.
Gently fold all ingredients together until well combined. Do not overmix to maintain some avocado chunks.
Taste the dip and adjust salt or lime juice as needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Ukrainian Potato & Bean Bites
recipes.visual_description: The Ukrainian Potato & Bean Bites are presented on a rustic, well-used wooden serving board, reminiscent of a family kitchen table. Small, round potato pancakes, about 5 cm in diameter, are golden-brown and slightly crispy at the edges. Each "deruny" base is topped with a creamy, pale green dollop of white bean and avocado spread, its smooth texture contrasting with the grated potato base. A small sprig of vibrant green fresh dill rests casually on top of each canapé, providing a pop of color. The arrangement is natural and slightly asymmetrical, with 10-12 pieces casually placed on the board, some touching, some with small gaps, showcasing their homely appeal. The background is minimal, hinting at a cozy kitchen setting with warm, inviting light. Everyday ceramic plates and a folded linen napkin are subtly visible nearby, reinforcing the comfort food aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of sour cream (smetana) for dipping.
Present on a traditional wooden serving board or a simple ceramic plate common in Ukrainian homes.
Serve alongside other small Ukrainian appetizers like pickled vegetables.

ingredients.name: cannellini beans (or other white beans), rinsed and drained

instructions: Grate potatoes and onion finely. Squeeze out excess liquid using a clean kitchen towel.
Combine grated potato and onion with 2 minced garlic cloves, flour, egg, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper in a large bowl. Mix well.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Drop tablespoonfuls of potato mixture into the hot oil, flattening slightly to form small, round patties (about 4-5 cm diameter).
Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove potato bites and place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
In a food processor, combine drained white beans, avocado, 1 minced garlic clove, lemon juice, 5g chopped dill, olive oil, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper.
Process until smooth and creamy. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Place cooled potato bites on a serving platter.
Spoon or pipe a generous dollop of white bean and avocado topping onto each potato bite.
Garnish with a small sprig of fresh dill. Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: Grating potatoes and squeezing out liquid for "deruny" (potato pancakes)
Frying small patties until golden and crisp

recipes.recipe_name: Chilled Avocado-Chipotle Velouté with Cotija Espuma
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of chilled avocado-chipotle velouté is presented in a wide, shallow, modern bone china bowl with a matte white finish. The velouté, a vibrant, pale avocado green, forms a smooth, flowing pool at the base of the bowl, its surface pristine and reflective. Centrally placed on the velouté is a delicate, airy cloud of pure white cotija espuma, rising softly with an ethereal texture. Around the espuma, a few precise droplets of brilliant emerald green epazote oil are strategically placed, creating a subtle, artistic contrast. A single, tiny, vibrant green micro cilantro leaf or a fine, red chili thread rests delicately on the espuma, serving as the sole, precise garnish. The ample negative space of the bowl emphasizes the minimalism and elegance of the composition. The bowl rests on a polished white Carrara marble surface. A pristine, crisply folded white linen napkin is positioned to the side. Dramatic, professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures and colors. The background is ultra-minimalist, showcasing only the dish and refined table elements.

ingredients.name: Micro cilantro or a single chili thread

instructions: Prepare Epazote Oil: Blanch epazote leaves briefly. Immediately transfer to ice water. Squeeze dry. Blend blanched epazote with neutral oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth. Chill the oil.

Prepare Avocado-Chipotle Velouté: Halve avocados, remove pits, scoop flesh into a blender. Add vegetable stock, chipotle chile (remove seeds for less heat), lime juice, salt, and pepper. Blend until perfectly smooth and creamy. Pass the velouté through a fine-mesh sieve for an ultra-silky texture. Adjust seasoning. Chill thoroughly for at least 2 hours.

Prepare Cotija Espuma: In a small saucepan, combine cotija cheese, whole milk, and heavy cream. Heat gently until cheese melts and mixture is warm. Do not boil. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any solids. Pour the strained liquid into a culinary siphon. Charge with one N2O cartridge. Shake well. Keep warm in a bain-marie or at room temperature until serving.

Assemble and Serve: Pour the chilled avocado-chipotle velouté into the center of each chilled serving bowl. Dispense a cloud of cotija espuma onto the center of the velouté. Drizzle a few drops of epazote oil artfully around the espuma. Garnish with a single, delicate micro cilantro leaf or a fine chili thread. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato & Pea Terrine with Aged Cheddar Mousse
recipes.visual_description: The dish, a study in refined minimalism, rests on an elegant bone china plate upon a polished grey-veined Carrara marble surface, lit by dramatic professional lighting. Two or three precisely cut, firm rectangular blocks of golden-brown potato terrine are arranged off-center. Its delicate, compressed potato layers reveal subtle onion and oregano. Adjacent, a vibrant, emerald-green pea puree forms an organic, smooth curve. Small, airy quenelles of pale yellow aged cheddar mousse are artfully placed. Two or three irregular, golden-brown crispy pasta shards stand vertically, providing sharp texture. A verdant, clear oregano oil is thoughtfully drizzled around components, creating an artistic, connecting pattern. A single, delicate sprig of fresh oregano or microgreen rests atop the terrine, adding a final fresh accent. Abundant negative space emphasizes deliberate placement and perfect execution, embodying sophisticated simplicity.

ingredients.name: Lasagna sheets or other flat pasta, broken into irregular pieces

instructions: Slice potatoes very thinly (1-2 mm thick). Layer potato slices, finely sliced onion, chopped oregano, salt, and pepper in a small, parchment-lined terrine mold or loaf pan (approx. 15x8 cm). Pour vegetable stock and olive oil over layers. Cover with foil. Bake at 160°C for 60-75 minutes, until potatoes are very tender. Place a weighted object on top to press while cooling. Chill completely for at least 4 hours, or overnight.

Bring a small pot of vegetable stock or water to a boil. Add green peas and blanch for 2 minutes. Drain immediately. Transfer peas to a high-speed blender with butter and a splash of stock. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for an ultra-silky texture. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Gently heat 100 ml heavy cream in a small saucepan. Add grated cheddar and stir until melted and smooth. Do not boil. Cool slightly. Whip remaining 50 ml heavy cream to soft peaks. Fold cooled cheese mixture into whipped cream. Season with salt and cayenne if desired. Transfer to a piping bag or small bowl.
Heat vegetable oil in a small pot to 170°C. Fry pasta pieces in batches until golden brown and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Season lightly with sea salt.
Combine extra virgin olive oil and fresh oregano leaves in a small blender. Blend until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth for a clear, vibrant oil.

Unmold the chilled potato terrine. Carefully slice into 1.5-2 cm thick rectangles or squares. Place one or two potato terrine pieces off-center on each plate. Artistically spoon or pipe pea puree alongside the terrine. Add small dollops or quenelles of aged cheddar mousse. Arrange 2-3 crispy pasta shards vertically or diagonally. Drizzle oregano oil around the plate, connecting elements. Garnish with a tiny sprig of fresh oregano or a microgreen.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Poblano and Avocado Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Roasted Poblano and Avocado Salad is presented with sophisticated artistry on a modern designer white plate, featuring ample negative space. Diced roasted poblano, with its smoky green, is artfully arranged in a natural, flowing composition. Cubes of vibrant green avocado are nestled amongst the poblano. A silky, pale green tomatillo-cumin emulsion pools elegantly around the components. Two delicate, crisp cotija tuiles stand upright, adding height and a salty crunch. A few small, fresh cilantro leaves provide a final touch. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the thoughtful arrangement. The setting features a premium grey veined marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin, and a sleek silver fork. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows against an ultra-minimalist background, honoring contemporary Mexican cuisine.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side of warm, freshly made corn tortillas.
Offer a very small, elegant bowl of salsa macha for optional added depth.
instructions: Roast poblano chiles: Char chiles over an open flame or under a broiler until skin blackens. Place in a sealed bag for 10 minutes. Peel, deseed, and remove stems. Cut chiles into 1 cm dice.

Prepare tomatillo emulsion: Blanch tomatillos in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain. Blend tomatillos with lime juice, 5g ground cumin, 60ml olive oil, and a pinch of salt. Emulsify until very smooth. Pass the emulsion through a fine-mesh sieve for a refined texture.
Prepare cotija tuiles: Grate cotija cheese. Form thin 5 cm rounds on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake at 180°C for 5-7 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Cool completely on the sheet.
Prepare avocado: Cut avocados into clean 1.5 cm cubes. Season lightly with sea salt.

Assemble the salad: Artfully arrange the diced roasted poblano on each plate in a natural, flowing composition. Place avocado cubes precisely among the poblano. Drizzle the tomatillo emulsion around and over the components. Place 1-2 crisp cotija tuiles upright on each plate. Garnish with a few small, fresh cilantro leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Terrine with Pea Emulsion and Aged Cheddar Crisp
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine white Carrara marble surface, atop a modern, subtly patterned bone china plate. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the architectural precision and abundant negative space. The central feature is a composition of a few precisely cut 2x2cm cubes of compressed potato terrine, showcasing a dense, uniform texture. Adjacent to the terrine, a delicate, flowing 'swoosh' of vibrant green pea emulsion provides a soft, velvety contrast. Elegant, irregularly shaped golden-brown aged cheddar crisps are artfully placed, offering a textural counterpoint. A few translucent slivers of ruby-red pickled red onion are sparingly scattered for color and acidity. A small, artful cluster of tiny oregano pasta pearls adds a subtle textural element. The entire composition is minimalist, with each component intentionally positioned to create a sophisticated, organic arrangement. A few delicate microgreens or chervil sprigs serve as the sole, precise garnish. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests beside the plate, completing the ultra-sophisticated, restrained presentation.

ingredients.name: Microgreens or delicate herb sprigs (e.g., chervil, dill)

instructions: Prepare the Potato Terrine: Dice potatoes into 5mm cubes. Place in a saucepan, cover with cold salted water, and bring to a boil. Cook until just tender, about 8-10 minutes. Drain well. Return potatoes to the pan, add 50g butter and vegetable stock. Season with salt and pepper. Gently mash until mostly smooth but with some texture remaining. Press the potato mixture firmly into a lined rectangular mould (approx. 15x8cm). Chill for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, until very firm.

Prepare the Pea Emulsion: Blanch green peas in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well. Blend peas, double cream, and mint leaves until very smooth. Pass the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to achieve a velvety emulsion. Season with salt. Keep chilled.

Prepare the Aged Cheddar Crisps: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Arrange small mounds (approx. 5g each) of grated cheddar on the parchment, spaced apart. Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Remove from oven and let cool completely on the parchment. They will crisp up as they cool.

Prepare the Pickled Red Onion: In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat and add thinly sliced red onion. Let steep for at least 30 minutes. Drain before serving.

Prepare the Oregano Pasta Pearls: Cook orzo pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain well. In a small pan, melt 15g butter. Add chopped fresh oregano and stir for 30 seconds. Toss the cooked orzo with the oregano butter. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Assemble the Dish: Carefully unmould the chilled potato terrine. Cut into precise 2x2cm cubes or elegant rectangular batons. On each plate, create a delicate 'swoosh' or an artistic dollop of the pea emulsion. Arrange 2-3 pieces of potato terrine artfully on or next to the pea emulsion, allowing for generous negative space. Place 1-2 aged cheddar crisps elegantly beside the terrine. Scatter a few drained pickled red onion slivers sparingly. Place a small, artful cluster of oregano pasta pearls. Garnish with a few microgreens or delicate herb sprigs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Buckwheat Tuiles, Silken Tofu Crémeux, Ancho Chili Consommé Gel
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on an expansive, pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, organic ripple pattern. Abundant negative space surrounds a meticulously composed cluster of elements. A smooth, ethereal swirl of ivory Silken Tofu Crémeux anchors the composition, its surface gleaming softly. Adjacent, two or three irregularly shaped, golden-brown Buckwheat Tuile shards stand upright, showcasing their delicate, crisp texture. Scattered around the crémeux and tuiles are a few jewel-like, translucent cubes of deep ruby-red Ancho Chili Consommé Gel, catching the light. A few precise drops of vibrant red Chili Oil are strategically placed on the crémeux, adding a pop of intense color. The entire arrangement is crowned with a whisper of fresh, bright green micro cilantro, providing a final touch of verdant contrast. The lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows that emphasize the dish's architectural precision and textural interplay. The background is ultra-minimalist, hinting at a premium grey marble surface.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Whisk melted butter, egg whites, and sugar.
Sift buckwheat flour, all-purpose flour, and salt into mixture. Whisk until smooth.
Spread thin layers of batter onto a silicone mat using an offset spatula.
Bake 8-10 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Cool on a wire rack. Break into irregular, elegant shards.
Combine silken tofu, soy milk, rice vinegar, salt, and white pepper in a high-speed blender.
Blend until perfectly smooth and creamy.
Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to chill and firm slightly.
Toast ancho chiles lightly in a dry pan until fragrant. Do not burn.
Rehydrate chiles in hot water for 15 minutes. Discard water.
Blend rehydrated chiles with vegetable stock until smooth.
Pass mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. This is your "consommé."
Bring consommé to a simmer. Whisk in agar-agar and smoked paprika. Simmer 1 minute, whisking constantly.
Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set, about 30 minutes.
Once set, cut into small, irregular cubes or break into delicate shards.
Heat neutral oil in a small saucepan over low heat.
Add dried red chili flakes. Infuse for 10 minutes. Do not let flakes burn.
Strain oil, discarding flakes. Let cool.
Spoon a dollop of Silken Tofu Crémeux onto one side of each plate, creating an organic swirl.
Arrange 2-3 Buckwheat Tuile shards artfully around the crémeux.
Place a few pieces of Ancho Chili Consommé Gel alongside.
Drizzle a few drops of Chili Oil sparingly over the crémeux and gel.
Garnish with a few micro cilantro or micro basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Warm Barley & Buckwheat Salad with Roasted Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of warm grain salad is elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. The composition features a balanced mound of earthy pearl barley, buckwheat groats, and bulgur wheat. Interspersed throughout are vibrant orange carrot cubes, creamy white parsnip cubes, and pale celeriac cubes, all roasted to a tender-crisp texture with slightly caramelized edges. A light, glossy beer-mustard vinaigrette coats the ingredients, providing a subtle sheen. The salad is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley, adding a pop of color and freshness. Moderate negative space surrounds the dish, highlighting the food. Traditional silver flatware is placed beside the plate on a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a professional yet approachable bistro atmosphere in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a crusty loaf of artisanal bread for dipping.
Can be offered as part of a selection of small plates or starters.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel carrots, parsnips, and celeriac. Cut into 1.5 cm cubes.
Toss cut vegetables with 2 tablespoons olive oil, fresh thyme, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast vegetables for 25-30 minutes. They should be tender and slightly caramelized.
Rinse pearl barley. Cook in 400 ml vegetable stock according to package instructions, about 25-30 minutes. Drain excess liquid.
Rinse buckwheat groats and bulgur. Cook in remaining 400 ml vegetable stock for 10-15 minutes, or until tender. Drain well.
Finely dice the shallot. In a small bowl, whisk together light ale, Dijon mustard, apple cider vinegar, remaining 3 tablespoons olive oil, diced shallot, salt, and pepper to make the vinaigrette.
In a large bowl, combine the warm cooked barley, buckwheat, bulgur, and roasted vegetables. Gently mix.
Pour the vinaigrette over the warm grain and vegetable mixture. Toss gently to coat.
Portion the warm salad onto individual plates. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Buckwheat-Crusted Delicata Squash, Almond, Mustard Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly round buckwheat-crusted delicata squash medallion anchors the center of a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, delicate pattern. The squash exhibits a rich golden-orange interior with a dark, crisp, textured buckwheat and panko crust. Beneath the medallion, a small, artfully placed pool of glossy, golden-brown mustard reduction provides a sophisticated base. Around the squash, a scattering of toasted slivered almonds adds a light, contrasting texture and a warm, nutty hue. A few vibrant green microgreens are precisely placed for a delicate pop of color and freshness. The composition embraces abundant negative space. The dish rests on a premium grey veined marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates soft shadows. A meticulously folded white linen napkin sits beside the plate, complementing the ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Wash squash. Slice squash into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Remove seeds.
Toss squash rounds with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp. Cool slightly.
Spread buckwheat groats on a separate baking sheet. Toast in oven for 8-10 minutes until fragrant and lightly browned. Let cool.
Pulse toasted buckwheat groats and panko breadcrumbs in a food processor until a coarse, even crumb forms. Season with a pinch of salt.
Lightly coat each squash medallion in the buckwheat-breadcrumb mixture, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Sear crusted squash medallions for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crisp. Set aside.
