Deglazing pan to create a rich sauce

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Yam Purée and Parmesan Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, refined composition on a pristine white bone china plate with generous negative space. An elegant, organic sweep of vibrant orange yam purée forms the base. Centered atop the purée are two or three thick, perfectly seared golden-brown chicken breast pieces, showcasing a tender, juicy interior. A delicate, irregular golden-brown parmesan tuile leans artfully against the chicken, adding architectural height and a crisp texture. A few crisp, dark green fried oregano leaves are precisely scattered for color contrast and aromatic garnish. The plate rests on a premium white Carrara marble surface. A precisely folded white linen napkin is positioned beside the plate. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, enhancing depth and highlighting the dish's sophisticated simplicity. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a single, perfectly portioned serving.
instructions: Prepare yam purée. Peel yam. Dice into 2cm cubes. Steam or boil yam until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.

Finely mince shallot and garlic. In a small saucepan, melt 10g butter over medium heat. Sauté minced shallot and garlic until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add cooked yam and 50ml chicken stock. Mash thoroughly or blend with an immersion blender until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare parmesan tuiles. Grate parmesan cheese finely. On a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, form 5cm diameter circles of grated parmesan, leaving space between each. Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for 5-7 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Cool on the baking sheet; they will crisp further.

Prepare fried oregano. Heat vegetable oil in a small saucepan to 170°C. Carefully add fresh oregano leaves or small sprigs. Fry briefly, about 10-15 seconds, until crisp and vibrant green. Do not overcrowd. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.

Prepare chicken. Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper. Heat olive oil and 20g butter in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat until butter foams.

Place chicken breasts in the hot pan. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until deeply golden brown. Transfer the pan to a preheated oven at 190°C. Cook for 8-10 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Transfer chicken to a cutting board. Rest for 5 minutes.

Plate the dish. Spoon a generous, elegant swirl or organic dollop of warm yam purée onto the center of each white bone china plate. Slice each rested chicken breast into two or three thick, clean pieces (do not fan). Arrange the chicken pieces artfully on top of the yam purée.

Lean one delicate parmesan tuile against the chicken. Scatter a few crisp, dark green fried oregano leaves precisely around the chicken and purée. Drizzle a few drops of sesame oil sparingly around the plated elements. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken, Cured Ham, and Mushroom Soup
recipes.visual_description: The hearty soup is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl, showcasing a rich, golden-amber broth. Visible within are generous, evenly diced pieces of tender chicken, small, savory cubes of cured ham, and earthy, thinly sliced cremini mushrooms. A delicate layer of freshly grated Parmesan cheese melts gently on the surface, its white contrasting with the vibrant green of finely chopped fresh parsley scattered over the top. The ingredients are well-distributed, creating a balanced and appealing composition with clear negative space around the bowl. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and classic silver flatware beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the soup's warm tones and inviting textures, emphasizing a clean, professional, yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2 cm cubes. Dice cured ham into 1 cm cubes. Thinly slice mushrooms.
Peel and finely dice the onion, carrot, and celery. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add diced chicken. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned on all sides. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add diced cured ham and sliced mushrooms to the pot. Cook 3-5 minutes until mushrooms soften.
Pour in chicken broth and beef broth. Bring soup to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Grate Parmesan cheese.
Ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish each portion with grated Parmesan and chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Sausage Jambalaya
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Chicken and Sausage Jambalaya fills a clean white porcelain bowl. The robust, reddish-brown rice is fluffy, speckled with vibrant diced red and green bell peppers and tender diced onion. Substantial golden-brown chicken chunks are scattered throughout, alongside well-caramelized rounds of smoked sausage. A light sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green onions and parsley adds a bright green contrast to the rich colors. The dish is presented on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed neatly beside the bowl. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the rustic, comforting textures. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere, with a small bottle of Louisiana-style hot sauce positioned discreetly.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of hot sauce for added spice.
Offer with crusty French bread for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Brown chicken in batches until golden. Remove chicken from pot.
Slice smoked sausage into 1 cm thick rounds. Add sausage to pot. Cook until browned. Remove sausage.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, bell peppers, and celery. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in Cajun seasoning, dried thyme, and bay leaves.
Return chicken and sausage to the pot.
Add diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in long-grain rice. Ensure rice is fully submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot tightly. Simmer 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not lift lid during cooking.
Remove pot from heat. Let stand covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Discard bay leaves.
Taste and adjust salt and black pepper as needed.
Garnish with fresh sliced green onions and chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For a spicier jambalaya, add a pinch of cayenne pepper with the Cajun seasoning.

recipes.recipe_name: Vietnamese Seared Pork Noodle Salad
recipes.visual_description: Seared pork medallions, golden-brown, are artfully arranged atop a bed of soft rice vermicelli noodles. Thinly shredded green lettuce and julienned cucumber provide a fresh base. Vibrant fresh Vietnamese basil leaves and thinly sliced red onion are scattered over the dish, adding color and aromatic freshness. Sliced black olives are interspersed, offering a briny counterpoint. A light drizzle of clear Nuoc Cham dressing lightly coats the ingredients, with a small pool at the bottom of the white porcelain bowl. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with chopsticks resting beside the bowl, and a small ceramic spoon. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh colors and textures. A cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the setting. The background is a subtle, casual restaurant blur.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side dish of extra Nuoc Cham for dipping.
Offer fresh chili slices or chili garlic sauce for added heat.
instructions: Slice pork loin into 1 cm thick medallions. Season with a pinch of sugar and black pepper. Set aside.
Prepare Nuoc Cham: Combine fish sauce, 60 ml warm water, sugar, lime juice, minced garlic, and sliced chili (if using). Stir until sugar dissolves. Set aside.
Cook rice vermicelli according to package directions. Rinse with cold water. Drain well. Set aside.

Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions 3-4 minutes per side. Cook until golden brown and cooked through. Remove from skillet. Let rest, then slice into thick chunks.
Thinly shred lettuce. Julienne cucumber. Thinly slice red onion. Halve or thinly slice black olives.
To assemble each starter bowl: Place a small bed of shredded lettuce and julienned cucumber at the bottom of a white porcelain bowl. Add a portion of rice vermicelli noodles.
Arrange pork chunks over the noodles. Scatter thinly sliced red onion, fresh basil leaves, and sliced black olives over the dish.
Spoon a generous amount of Nuoc Cham dressing over the ingredients. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure pork is cooked through but remains tender. Avoid overcooking.
The Nuoc Cham dressing provides the essential sweet, sour, salty, and spicy balance.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Kimchi Chicken Toasts
recipes.visual_description: Spicy Kimchi Chicken Toasts are presented generously on a rustic wooden board or a simple ceramic platter, reflecting a homestyle, unpretentious snack. Four thick slices of golden-brown, crisply toasted bread serve as the base. Each slice is piled high with a rich, vibrant mixture of finely diced chicken and bright red-orange chopped kimchi, interspersed with finely diced onion and grated carrot. The chicken is cooked to a tender, juicy texture, contrasting with the crisp bread. A light sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds or finely chopped spring onion adds a final touch of color and texture. The arrangement is casual, with some filling spilling naturally, suggesting abundance and comfort. The scene is set on a well-used wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, natural light, with everyday ceramic plates and a casually placed cloth napkin in the background, emphasizing a relaxed family dining atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Toasted sesame seeds or chopped spring onion

instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add finely diced chicken. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add finely diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and thinly sliced chili. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped kimchi and grated carrot. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Return cooked chicken to the pan. Add soy sauce and gochujang (if using). Stir well to combine.
Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Remove from heat. Stir in sesame oil.
Toast bread slices until golden brown and crisp.
Spoon generous amounts of the kimchi chicken mixture onto each toasted bread slice.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds or chopped spring onion, if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken, Roasted Yam Puree, Tomato Confit
recipes.visual_description: A pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and glistening, rests off-center on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant pattern. The chicken, presented as a whole, succulent piece, anchors the composition. Adjacent to it, a sweeping, organic smear of vibrant orange roasted yam puree provides a warm color base. Nestled artfully on the puree, a cluster of glossy, slightly burst confit cherry tomatoes adds pops of deep red, their skins gently wrinkled. Scattered around the chicken and puree are a few deeply caramelized pearl onions, their rich brown hues contrasting with the brighter elements. A delicate drizzle of emerald-green oregano-infused olive oil, with a hint of sesame oil, creates an abstract pattern across the plate and around the components, adding aroma and sheen. The plate is set on a light grey veined marble surface. A folded white linen napkin, a single elegant fork, and a small, understated water glass occupy the vast negative space, emphasizing the dish's minimalist sophistication. Dramatic, professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty artisanal bread for dipping in the infused oil.
A light, crisp green salad with a simple vinaigrette.
instructions: Prepare oregano oil: Gently heat 40ml olive oil with dried oregano sticks in a small saucepan over low heat for 15 minutes. Do not let it fry. Strain and set aside.
Roast yam: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel yam. Cut into 2cm cubes. Toss with 5ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until very tender.

Make yam puree: Transfer roasted yam to a blender. Add butter, 50ml chicken stock, and a pinch of salt. Blend until perfectly smooth and creamy. Adjust consistency with more stock if needed. Keep warm.

Confit tomatoes: In a small oven-safe dish, combine cherry tomatoes, 5ml olive oil, smashed unpeeled garlic cloves, and thyme sprigs. Season lightly with salt. Roast in the same 200°C oven for 15-20 minutes until tomatoes are softened and slightly burst.

Caramelize pearl onions: Peel pearl onions. Heat a small pan over medium-low heat. Add 5ml olive oil. Add pearl onions. Cook slowly for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and tender. A splash of water can help deglaze.

Sear chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Add a splash of olive oil. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip. Cook for another 6-8 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure yam puree is perfectly smooth. Pass through a sieve if necessary for ultra-fine dining texture.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing chicken to ensure a good crust.
Resting the chicken is crucial for juiciness.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo Estilo Casero
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Arroz con Pollo is presented on a clean, round white ceramic plate. Vibrant orange-red rice, moist and slightly saucy, forms a rustic mound. Nestled atop is a single, perfectly seared chicken thigh, its skin golden-brown and crisp, meat tender. Bright green peas are scattered throughout the rice, adding pops of color. Fresh, chopped cilantro garnishes the dish. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and a small rustic basket with warm corn tortillas are beside it. A small ceramic bowl of red salsa roja sits nearby. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and inviting textures. The presentation is clean, professional, and authentically Mexican, designed for casual yet refined dining.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas.
Offer a side of salsa roja.
Include lime wedges for squeezing over the dish.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, oregano, chili powder, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to the pot. Stir well to coat rice with vegetables and spices. Cook for 2-3 minutes, toasting the rice slightly.
If using fresh tomatoes, blend them until smooth. Add blended fresh tomatoes or canned crushed tomatoes to the pot. Stir and cook for 5 minutes, allowing moisture to evaporate slightly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the rice mixture. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in frozen green peas and chopped fresh cilantro. Cover and let stand for 5 minutes off heat.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning.
notes: For a spicier dish, add a diced jalapeño or serrano pepper with the bell peppers.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken, Kimchi Emulsion, Roasted Carrot, Garlic-Chili Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of meticulously plated pan-seared chicken, presented on an elegant matte white or light grey ceramic plate. The golden-brown, perfectly seared chicken breast is positioned as the focal point, its surface exhibiting a delicate crust. Adjacent to the chicken, a vibrant, smooth, deep red kimchi emulsion forms an organic, flowing base, providing a striking color contrast. Two or three perfectly roasted baby carrots, retaining their vibrant orange hue and slight caramelization, are artfully placed next to the chicken. A minimal, artistic scattering of golden-brown garlic-chili crumble adds a textural counterpoint. The dish is sparingly garnished with a few tiny, fresh green oregano leaves, offering a subtle pop of color and freshness. The overall composition emphasizes abundant negative space, showcasing each element with architectural precision. The plate rests on a premium, light-colored marble surface, accompanied by a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Subtle, modern, dark grey chopsticks are positioned to the side, hinting at the dish's Korean inspiration. Dramatic, focused lighting creates soft shadows, enhancing the dish's three-dimensional quality and sophisticated simplicity.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Wash and peel baby carrots. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized. Set aside.

For the kimchi emulsion: Finely mince shallot and 2 garlic cloves. Coarsely chop kimchi. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Sauté shallot until translucent, about 2 minutes. Add minced garlic and chopped kimchi. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Deglaze with chicken stock and rice vinegar. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes to reduce slightly. Transfer mixture to a high-speed blender. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Keep warm.

For the garlic-chili crumble: Roughly chop stale bread. Pulse in a food processor to coarse crumbs. Finely mince remaining 2 garlic cloves and red chili. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and chili. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Add bread crumbs. Toast, stirring frequently, until golden brown and crispy. Season with salt. Set aside.

Prepare chicken: Pat chicken breasts very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.

Place chicken breasts skin-side down (if skin-on, otherwise presentation side down). Sear 4-5 minutes until deep golden brown and a crust forms. Flip chicken. Add butter to the pan. Baste chicken with melted butter. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from oven. Rest on a cutting board 5 minutes before plating.

To plate: Spoon a generous pool of warm kimchi emulsion onto the center of each plate, creating an organic sweep. Place one whole pan-seared chicken breast artistically atop the emulsion. Arrange 3 roasted baby carrots beside the chicken. Sprinkle garlic-chili crumble sparingly over the chicken and around the plate for texture. Garnish with a few small, fresh oregano leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Torta al Limone e Semi di Papavero (Senza Glutine, Senza Lattosio)
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of golden-yellow cake is presented on a simple, round, white ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge. The cake has a fine, moist crumb visible on the cut side, dotted generously with small, dark poppy seeds. A thin, slightly opaque white lemon glaze cascades gently over the top surface of the slice, pooling slightly at the base. A small, fresh lemon wedge rests casually beside the cake slice on the plate. In the blurred background, the remaining whole cake, round and fully glazed, sits on a worn wooden cutting board or a simple cake stand. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table. Lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy kitchen atmosphere. A loosely folded, light-colored linen napkin is placed nearby. The overall impression is one of comforting, homemade Italian dessert.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small cup of freshly brewed espresso.
Enjoy as an afternoon snack (merenda) or after a light meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake tin with rice flour.
In a large bowl, whisk together rice flour, granulated sugar, poppy seeds, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk eggs, olive oil, 60 ml lemon juice, lemon zest, and vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into prepared cake tin.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove cake from oven. Let cool in the tin for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
For the glaze, whisk icing sugar with 15-30 ml lemon juice until smooth. Adjust consistency with more juice if needed.
Once cake is cool, pour glaze over the top. Let glaze set before serving.
notes: Ensure all ingredients are at room temperature for best results.
Do not overmix the batter to keep the cake tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Steamed Chicken Breast, Avocado Crème, Compressed Yam, Tomato Essence, Parmesan Garlic Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of a Michelin-starred dish presented on an exquisite, large, bone china plate with a wide, pristine white rim. The composition is elegantly asymmetrical and organic, celebrating abundant negative space. A perfectly steamed and lightly seared chicken medallion, showcasing a delicate golden crust and moist interior, rests slightly off-center. Beside it, a silken, pale green quenelle of avocado crème, its surface impossibly smooth, adds a soft, luxurious counterpoint. A precise, golden-orange rectangle of compressed yam confit is positioned to balance the plate, its subtle sear visible. Several translucent, vibrant red cubes of tomato essence gel are scattered artfully, providing bursts of color and acidity. A delicate, golden-brown parmesan-garlic crisp, with an irregular, organic shape, stands vertically or lies delicately, offering a textural contrast. The plate is garnished with a minimal scattering of bright green, finely sliced chives. The setting is a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates subtle shadows, emphasizing the dish's architectural precision. A pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded into a triangle, sits to the side. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the dish remains the absolute focal point.
instructions: Prepare Chicken: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Steam chicken for 15-18 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken. Cut into 4 thick medallions.

Make Avocado Crème: Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Add whole avocados. Boil for 5-7 minutes until very soft. Drain and cool slightly. Scoop avocado flesh into a high-speed blender. Add 15ml olive oil and pinch of salt. Blend until ultra-smooth and silken. Pass through a fine mesh sieve for ultimate refinement. Keep warm.

Prepare Compressed Yam: Peel and dice yams into 2cm cubes. Melt butter in a pan. Add yams, salt, and white pepper. Cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until very tender, about 20-25 minutes. Mash lightly. Press the cooked yam mixture into a small, parchment-lined rectangular mold. Chill under pressure for at least 2 hours. Cut into 4 precise rectangles.

Create Tomato Essence Gel: Roughly chop tomatoes and shallot. Combine with thyme in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat until tomatoes break down, about 15 minutes. Strain mixture through a fine mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Gently heat the clear tomato liquid. Whisk in agar-agar until dissolved. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set. Cut into small, precise cubes or spheres.

Bake Parmesan Garlic Crisp: Preheat oven to 160°C. Mix grated Parmesan with minced garlic. Spread a very thin layer onto a parchment-lined baking sheet, forming irregular, delicate shapes. Bake for 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely.
Sear Yam and Chicken: Heat a non-stick pan with a touch of neutral oil. Sear yam rectangles on all sides until golden. Briefly sear chicken medallions for a light crust.

Plate Dish: Place one seared chicken medallion slightly off-center on a pristine white plate. Spoon a quenelle of avocado crème beside it. Arrange one seared yam rectangle elegantly. Place a few tomato essence gel cubes artfully. Finish with a delicate parmesan garlic crisp. Garnish with a sprinkle of finely sliced chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Corn Broth with Zero-Waste Greens
recipes.visual_description: A minimalistic and clean presentation of a clear, light golden broth in a handcrafted, unglazed cream-colored ceramic bowl. At the bottom of the bowl, bright yellow, plump fermented corn kernels are naturally scattered. A small, intentional cluster of finely chopped green garnishes, including delicate corn silk and vibrant spring onion greens, rests gently atop the corn. The composition emphasizes natural textures and colors, with ample white space around the liquid. The bowl sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed natural linen napkin. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the pure beauty of the ingredients. The background is clean and simple, with a hint of natural greenery, maintaining a focus on sustainable simplicity.

ingredients.name: Mixed vegetable scraps (carrot peels, onion skins, celery ends, mushroom stems)
Finely chopped fresh parsley or cilantro stems

instructions: Combine corn kernels, 5g sea salt, and 250ml filtered water in a clean glass jar. Ensure kernels are fully submerged. Seal loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess. Burp daily if sealed. Refrigerate once fermented.
Place corn cobs and mixed vegetable scraps in a large pot. Add 2 litres of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes.
Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding all solids. Season broth with 2g sea salt.
Gently warm the zero-waste broth in a saucepan. Do not boil vigorously.
Ladle warm broth into four individual ceramic bowls. Add 30-40g of fermented corn kernels to each bowl.
Finely chop corn silk, spring onion greens, and parsley/cilantro stems. Sprinkle a small, neat cluster of this zero-waste garnish over the center of the corn kernels in each bowl. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chicken & Potato Croquettes with Umami Mushroom Ketchup
recipes.visual_description: A collection of golden-brown, irregularly shaped croquettes are arranged artfully on a light cream-colored handcrafted ceramic plate, leaving generous negative space. Each croquette, roughly cylindrical and about 5cm long, boasts a slightly textured, crispy exterior from frying. The color palette is earthy and warm: the deep golden-brown of the croquettes contrasts with the rich, dark brown of the accompanying mushroom ketchup. A small, organic dollop of the smooth, glossy Umami Mushroom Ketchup sits beside the croquettes, reflecting light subtly. The plating emphasizes natural forms and simple elegance. No garnishes are used, highlighting the pure beauty of the ingredients. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood surface. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, casting gentle shadows and enhancing the organic textures. The background is clean and minimalist, featuring a hint of natural plant greenery, reinforcing the sustainable theme.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Garlic Paste: Blend 100g peeled garlic cloves with 100ml non-chlorinated water and 2g sea salt. Transfer to a clean jar. Ferment 5-7 days at room temperature until tangy. Refrigerate.

Make Umami Mushroom Ketchup: Roughly chop 200g mushrooms. In a saucepan, combine mushrooms, 150ml water, 15ml light soy sauce, 10ml rice vinegar, and 5g brown sugar. Simmer 20-25 minutes until mushrooms are very soft. Blend until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve.

Prepare Croquette Mixture: Combine 300g shredded cooked chicken, 400g mashed potatoes, 15g fermented garlic paste, and 30g sun-dried tomato paste in a large bowl. Add 30g potato starch, salt, and pepper. Mix well to form a cohesive dough.
Form Croquettes: Shape 30g portions of mixture into small cylinders or spheres.
Fry Croquettes: Heat neutral oil to 170°C (340°F). Fry croquettes in batches 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Drain.
Serve: Arrange croquettes on a plate. Serve immediately with Umami Mushroom Ketchup.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef with Orange-Chocolate Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of perfectly seared beef, presented as a whole, thick piece, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The beef boasts a rich, deep brown crust from searing, contrasting with its tender, rosy interior. A glossy, amber-orange reduction sauce, infused with dark chocolate, is artfully spooned over the beef, creating a vibrant sheen. Beside the beef, a neat cluster of bright green beans, steamed to a tender-crisp, and a few whole, vibrant orange baby carrots provide a fresh counterpoint of color and texture. A sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the beef, adding a touch of herbaceous green. The plate features moderate negative space, highlighting the dish's balanced composition. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, all bathed in natural, even lighting.
instructions: Pat beef dry with paper towels. Season all sides generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place beef into hot pan. Sear 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until internal temperature reaches 60-65°C. For well-done, cook to 75°C.
Remove beef from pan. Place on a cutting board. Cover loosely with foil. Let rest 5-7 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium. Add shallots to pan drippings. Sauté 2 minutes until softened. Add garlic. Sauté 1 minute more.
Pour in red wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of pan. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half.
Add beef stock and orange juice. Bring to a gentle simmer.
In a small bowl, whisk plain flour with 30 ml cold water to form a smooth slurry. Gradually whisk slurry into simmering sauce. Stir constantly until sauce thickens slightly.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in orange zest and chopped dark chocolate until chocolate is fully melted and sauce is smooth.
Stir in butter and fresh thyme sprigs. Taste sauce. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
While sauce reduces, steam or blanch green beans and baby carrots until tender-crisp. Drain well.
To serve, place one whole seared beef piece on each plate. Spoon generous amount of orange-chocolate reduction over beef.
Arrange a portion of green beans and baby carrots neatly beside beef. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Refined Pork and Chicken Consommé with Poached Chicken and Confit Potato
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, wide, shallow white bone china bowl centers the composition on a premium grey veined marble surface. Abundant negative space surrounds the elegantly presented consommé. The crystal-clear, deep amber consommé forms the base. Nestled within are precise 1.5 cm cubes of pale white poached chicken breast and creamy yellow confit potato, arranged organically in the bowl's center. A single, irregularly shaped brown rice and Parmesan crisp, golden-brown and delicate, rests artfully at the rim. A few precise droplets of vibrant red chili-garlic oil dot the consommé's surface, providing a subtle color contrast. Two or three tiny, fresh green micro dill sprigs are placed delicately alongside the main elements, adding a final touch of fresh color. The scene is lit with dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sophisticated minimalism. A perfectly folded white linen napkin and simple, elegant silver flatware complete the refined setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small dollop of high-quality smetana (sour cream) on the side for those who wish to add it, presented in a small, elegant spoon.
Accompany with a thin slice of Borodinsky bread (dark rye bread) if desired, served on a separate small plate.
instructions: Prepare Broth: Place roasted pork bones, chicken wings, quartered onion, smashed garlic, carrots, celery, peppercorns, and bay leaf in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Bring slowly to a simmer. Skim any foam. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 4-6 hours. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Discard solids. Season broth with salt. Chill completely.

Clarify Broth (Consommé): In a large bowl, combine ground chicken, egg whites, finely diced onion, carrot, and celery. Mix well. Gently whisk this "raft" mixture into the chilled broth. Place pot over medium-low heat. Stir constantly until raft begins to form and float to the top. Stop stirring. Create a small "chimney" in the raft for steam to escape. Simmer very gently for 45-60 minutes. The broth should be clear. Carefully ladle the clear consommé through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth, avoiding disturbing the raft. Keep warm.

Poach Chicken: Season chicken breast with salt and white pepper. Gently poach in simmering water or chicken broth until internal temperature reaches 75°C. This takes about 10-15 minutes depending on thickness. Cool slightly. Cut chicken into small, precise cubes (approx. 1.5 cm).

Prepare Confit Potato: Cut peeled potato into small, precise cubes (approx. 1.5 cm). Place potato cubes, neutral oil, smashed garlic, thyme, and salt in a small saucepan. Heat gently over very low heat. Cook until potatoes are tender but hold their shape, about 20-30 minutes. Do not fry. Drain potatoes.

Make Brown Rice & Parmesan Crisp: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Mix cooked brown rice, grated Parmesan, and a pinch of salt. Spread mixture very thinly in an irregular, organic shape (approx. 8x10 cm) on the parchment paper. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Cool on a wire rack.
Prepare Chili-Garlic Oil: Heat neutral oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add sliced garlic and chili flakes. Gently infuse for 5-7 minutes. Do not brown garlic. Strain oil, discarding solids.

Assemble Dish: Gently warm the cubed chicken and confit potato. Place precise amounts of chicken cubes and potato cubes artfully in the bottom of a wide, shallow soup bowl. Carefully ladle the hot, clear consommé around the elements, filling the bowl about halfway. Place one brown rice and Parmesan crisp delicately on the side of the bowl or slightly submerged. Drizzle a few drops of chili-garlic oil over the consommé. Garnish with a few micro dill sprigs. Serve immediately.
notes: Achieving a truly clear consommé requires patience and careful simmering.
The brown rice and Parmesan crisp adds textural contrast and a hint of umami, elevating the traditional broth.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Truffled Potato Purée and Dill Oil
recipes.visual_description: A refined pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and plump, rests slightly off-center on a large, pristine white bone china plate. Adjacent, a graceful quenelle of silky, off-white truffled potato purée is artfully placed, its smooth texture contrasting with the chicken's seared surface. A few deliberate droplets and a thin, swirling line of vibrant green dill oil encircle the chicken and purée, adding a splash of intense color and artistic flair. Two or three delicate, translucent potato tuile shards are meticulously positioned atop the purée, offering a textural counterpoint. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space highlighting the precise placement of each element. A few micro dill sprigs provide a final fresh garnish. The setting is a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's architectural precision and premium ingredients against an ultra-minimalist background, with a single refined restaurant portion presented.
instructions: Prepare dill oil: Blanch 20g dill briefly. Immediately shock in ice water. Squeeze dry. Blend dill with 50ml olive oil until smooth. Strain through a fine mesh sieve. Set aside.
Prepare herbed butter: Soften 50g butter. Finely chop 10g dill and mince garlic. Mix dill, garlic, salt, and pepper into butter. Form into a small log, wrap in cling film, chill until firm.
Prepare potato purée: Peel potatoes. Cut into 2cm cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender. Drain well. Pass potatoes through a ricer or fine mesh sieve into a warm saucepan.

Heat cream and milk. Add remaining 50g butter to riced potatoes. Gradually whisk in warm cream and milk until purée is silky smooth. Season with salt. Stir in truffle oil just before serving. Keep warm.

Prepare potato tuiles: Whisk potato starch with 50ml water until smooth. Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour a thin layer of starch mixture onto the hot pan to form small, irregular shapes. Cook until crisp and translucent. Carefully remove and let cool. Break into shards.

Prepare chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Make a deep pocket horizontally in each chicken breast without cutting through. Insert half of the chilled herbed butter into each pocket. Secure opening with toothpicks if needed.

Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Sear chicken breasts skin-side down (if skin-on) or presentation-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken for 5 minutes before plating.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Tomato and Feta Salad with Poached Eggs
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant composition. A generous bed of fresh, crisp green arugula forms the base. Scattered artfully across the arugula are plump, roasted cherry tomato halves, their skins slightly wrinkled and caramelized, revealing a deeper red hue. Interspersed among the tomatoes are delicate, thinly sliced rings of red onion, providing a subtle purple contrast. Crumbled white feta cheese is generously sprinkled over the vegetables, adding creamy texture and bright color. Each plate is crowned with a perfectly poached egg, its pristine white exterior holding a promise of a golden, runny yolk. A light drizzle of golden-green vinaigrette glistens over all components, enhancing their natural colors. The dish is arranged with a natural, organic flow, ensuring each ingredient is visible. The presentation is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, evoking a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 15-20 minutes until slightly softened and caramelized.
Prepare the dressing. In a small bowl, whisk remaining 45 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey, and dried oregano. Season with salt and pepper.

Poach the eggs. Fill a medium saucepan with water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add a splash of vinegar. Carefully crack each egg into a small ramekin. Gently slide eggs into simmering water. Cook for 3-4 minutes for runny yolks. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
Assemble the salad. In a large bowl, combine arugula, roasted tomatoes, and thinly sliced red onion. Drizzle with half the dressing. Toss gently to coat.
Divide salad among four plates. Top each portion with crumbled feta cheese. Place one poached egg on top of each salad. Drizzle with remaining dressing. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Saffron Corn Risotto and Roasted Pepper Coulis
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant portion of pan-seared chicken breast rests atop a vibrant, creamy saffron corn risotto on a pristine, matte white designer plate. The chicken, with its crisp, golden-brown skin, is cut into thick, succulent chunks, showcasing its moist interior. The risotto, a rich yellow hue from saffron and studded with bright corn kernels, flows organically on the plate, its creamy texture evident. A vibrant, smooth roasted red bell pepper and tomato coulis is artfully swiped across the plate, creating a contrasting pop of deep red. Precisely placed beside the risotto are a few tender, glazed orange carrot batons and crisp, blanched green broccoli florets. A delicate drizzle of emerald green basil oil completes the composition, adding a final touch of color and aroma. The dish is presented on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface with abundant negative space. Dramatic, professional lighting casts subtle shadows, highlighting the textures. A perfectly folded white linen napkin sits beside the plate, emphasizing the refined dining experience.

ingredients.name: Red bell peppers, roasted, peeled, deseeded

instructions: Prepare Saffron Corn Risotto: Warm chicken stock in a saucepan. Infuse saffron threads in a small amount of warm stock. In a separate large pan, melt 25g butter with 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Sauté diced shallots until translucent. Add Arborio rice; toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Pour in white wine; stir until absorbed. Begin adding warm stock, one ladle at a time, stirring continuously. Wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding more. After 10 minutes, stir in fresh corn kernels. Continue adding stock and stirring for 8-10 more minutes, until rice is al dente and creamy. Stir in remaining 25g butter, grated Parmesan, and saffron-infused stock. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and rest for 2 minutes.

Prepare Roasted Pepper & Tomato Coulis: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve bell peppers and tomatoes. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly charred. Cool, then peel bell peppers and tomatoes. In a blender, combine roasted bell peppers, tomatoes, 1 garlic clove, and 2 tbsp olive oil. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a refined texture. Season with salt.

Prepare Vegetables: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch broccoli florets for 2 minutes until tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well. In a small pan, boil baby carrots in salted water until tender. Drain. Glaze carrots in a separate pan with a knob of butter and a splash of water until slightly caramelized.

Prepare Basil Oil: Blanch basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched basil with 3 tbsp olive oil until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for clear oil.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in an oven-safe, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer pan to preheated 180°C oven. Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken for 5 minutes before slicing thick pieces.

Assemble Dish: Ladle a generous portion of Saffron Corn Risotto onto the center of each plate. Create a fluid, organic shape. Spoon Roasted Pepper & Tomato Coulis artfully around or beside the risotto. Place a few glazed carrot batons and blanched broccoli florets precisely on or next to the risotto. Arrange thick-cut pieces of seared chicken breast on top of the risotto. Drizzle sparingly with basil oil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Supreme, Potato Gratin, Mushroom-Dill Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly roasted chicken supreme, skin golden and crispy, rests gracefully on a premium bone china plate. Adjacent, a precisely cut rectangular portion of creamy potato gratin, its layers visible, offers a soft counterpoint. A rich, glossy mushroom-dill jus, deep amber-brown, pools elegantly beneath and around the chicken, its velvety texture inviting. Garnish is minimal: a few delicate, vibrant green dill fronds are artfully placed atop the gratin and near the chicken. The color palette is sophisticated, with warm golden browns, creamy whites, and deep earthy tones complemented by fresh green. Abundant negative space surrounds the central composition, emphasizing the dish's refined simplicity and precision.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side of quick-pickled cucumbers or a simple fresh dill salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Prepare potato gratin: Thinly slice potatoes (1-2mm). Mince 1 clove garlic. In a saucepan, gently heat cream with minced garlic, pinch of nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Do not boil. Arrange potato slices in a small oven-safe dish, layering and pouring cream mixture over each layer. Ensure potatoes are fully submerged. Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until tender and golden brown.

Prepare chicken: Pat chicken supremes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 5-7 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Add 20g butter to skillet. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

Prepare mushroom-dill jus: While chicken roasts, slice mushrooms and mince shallot and remaining garlic clove. In the same skillet (after removing chicken), add remaining butter. Sauté shallot and garlic for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add mushrooms. Cook until tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook until liquid is reduced by half and slightly thickened, about 10-15 minutes. Strain jus through a fine-mesh sieve for a smooth consistency. Stir in finely chopped fresh dill. Season with salt and pepper.

To serve: Cut the potato gratin into two precise rectangular portions. Place one portion on each plate. Position a roasted chicken supreme next to the gratin. Spoon the mushroom-dill jus artfully around the chicken and gratin. Garnish with a few small sprigs of fresh dill.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For the gratin, pressing down on the potatoes during baking helps achieve a denser, more cohesive texture.
traditional_techniques: Use of dill as a prominent herb
Incorporation of potato as a staple

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Fermented Noodle Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant salad presented on a minimalist, handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy tone, set on a light reclaimed wood surface. Cooked egg noodles form a loose, natural base. Diced fresh tomatoes, their red hues contrasting with the noodles, are scattered throughout. Interspersed are plump, whole lacto-fermented cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly taut, offering a deeper color. Grated cheese is lightly sprinkled over the top, adding a textural element. Fresh basil and parsley leaves provide bursts of green. The overall composition is clean and uncluttered, with ample white space, highlighting the natural beauty and varied textures of the ingredients. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish. An undyed linen napkin and simple wooden fork complete the eco-conscious setting.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomatoes: Gently prick 300g cherry tomatoes. Place in a clean jar with optional bay leaf and peppercorns. Dissolve 1 tsp non-iodized salt in 240ml filtered water to create a 2% brine. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring full submersion. Use a weight. Seal with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment 3-7 days at room temperature until tangy. Refrigerate.

Cook Noodles: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook 300g egg noodles to al dente according to package directions. Drain, reserving 100ml cooking water. Rinse noodles with cold water. Drain well.
Prepare Fresh Tomatoes: Dice the remaining 200g fresh tomatoes into 1cm cubes.
Prepare Cheese: Grate or crumble 100g cheese.
Make Dressing: Whisk 60ml reserved fermented tomato brine, 30ml extra virgin olive oil, and optional 15ml apple cider vinegar and 1 tsp Dijon mustard. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine Salad: In a large bowl, combine cooled noodles, diced fresh tomatoes, 2 minced garlic cloves, 30g chopped basil, and 15g chopped parsley. Add the fermented tomatoes.
Dress and Serve: Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently. Add grated/crumbled cheese. Toss lightly. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Herb Parmesan Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A creamy, free-flowing Parmesan risotto forms the base on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The Arborio rice is al dente, infused with fresh thyme and rosemary, showcasing a rich, off-white hue with vibrant green herb flecks. Thick slices of golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to perfection, are arranged neatly atop the risotto, not fanned. The chicken is juicy with a slight crisp exterior. A light sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and a few delicate sprigs of fresh thyme garnish the dish. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin, and traditional silver flatware, all under natural, even lighting, creating a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately upon completion, as risotto's creamy texture is best enjoyed fresh.
While often a 'primo piatto' (first course) in Italy, this is presented as a substantial main course.
instructions: Prepare ingredients. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Chop thyme and rosemary leaves. Grate parmesan.
Season chicken breasts generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 6-8 minutes per side until golden-brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Rest on a cutting board.
In the same pan, reduce heat to medium. Add butter. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges become translucent.
Pour in white wine (if using). Cook, stirring, until liquid is completely absorbed.

Add one ladle of warm chicken broth to the rice. Stir constantly until broth is absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed before adding the next. This process takes approximately 18-20 minutes.
When rice is creamy and al dente (still has a slight bite), stir in grated parmesan, chopped thyme, and chopped rosemary. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick pieces.
Serve risotto immediately in individual bowls or plates. Top each serving with sliced chicken. Garnish with a sprinkle of fresh parmesan or a small sprig of fresh herbs.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Risotto should be al dente and creamy, known as 'all'onda' (flowing or wavy).

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Breast, Sesame-Infused Risotto, Tomato Consommé, Avocado Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a large, round, matte white bone china plate with abundant negative space. A fluid, creamy mound of sesame-infused risotto anchors the composition. Two thick, seared chicken breast pieces, golden and crisp-skinned, contrast with tender interior. A small, clear pool of vibrant red tomato consommé glistens. Precise dots of pale green avocado emulsion offer creamy counterpoints. A delicate, golden-brown parmesan crisp stands elegantly, providing textural contrast. Finely chopped bright green chives and two halved red cherry tomatoes add pops of color. The organic, flowing, minimalist composition highlights natural forms. The plate rests on a smooth, cool grey marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded, sits to the side. Dramatic, soft professional lighting casts subtle shadows. An ultra-minimalist dark grey background ensures the dish remains the sole focus.
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Vacuum seal individually. Sous vide chicken at 63°C for 1.5 hours. Remove from bag. Pat dry thoroughly. Sear chicken in hot olive oil, skin-side down, until golden and crispy. Finish searing other side briefly. Rest.

Roughly chop tomatoes. Blend lightly. Strain tomato mixture through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Do not press. Collect clear liquid. Season with salt. Gently warm consommé just before serving.

Finely mince shallots and garlic. Sauté shallots in butter until translucent. Add garlic, cook 1 minute. Add rice. Toast 2 minutes. Deglaze with white wine. Cook until absorbed. Add hot chicken stock, ladle by ladle, stirring constantly. Add next ladle when previous is absorbed. Cook until rice is al dente, about 18-20 minutes. Stir in 80g grated Parmesan and toasted sesame oil. Season. Risotto should be fluid and creamy.
Scoop avocado flesh into a blender. Add a pinch of salt and a few drops of hot sauce. Blend until perfectly smooth and emulsified. Pass through a fine sieve.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grate 30g Parmesan finely. Arrange small mounds (approx. 5g each) on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool.

Place a generous spoon of risotto slightly off-center on each plate. Slice chicken breast into 2-3 thick, clean pieces. Arrange next to risotto. Do not fan. Spoon a small pool of warm tomato consommé next to the chicken. Dot the plate with small amounts of avocado emulsion. Place a delicate parmesan crisp on top of the chicken or next to it. Garnish with finely chopped chives and 2-3 halved cherry tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken and Avocado Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, well-balanced individual serving is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. A base of fluffy, pearly white long-grain rice supports golden-brown pan-seared chicken cubes. Creamy green avocado slices are arranged beside bright red cherry tomato halves. A glossy orange-red hot sauce dressing lightly coats the ingredients. Delicate shavings of pale yellow parmesan cheese are scattered over the chicken and vegetables. Fresh green cilantro leaves are sprinkled as a final garnish, adding a pop of color. The entire bowl is centered on a simple light wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is folded beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating subtle shadows. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Rinse 300g long-grain rice. Combine with 600ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat. Let stand covered for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Cut 600g chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove from skillet.
In a small bowl, whisk together 30ml hot sauce, 15ml toasted sesame oil, juice from 1 lime, and 2 minced garlic cloves.
Halve 200g cherry tomatoes. Halve and pit 2 large ripe avocados. Slice each half into 1cm thick pieces.
Divide cooked rice among 4 serving bowls. Arrange cooked chicken, sliced avocado, and halved cherry tomatoes over the rice. Drizzle evenly with the prepared hot sauce mixture.
Using a vegetable peeler, shave 50g parmesan cheese over each bowl. Scatter 15g chopped fresh cilantro over the top.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked thoroughly to 75°C (167°F).
Adjust hot sauce to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Shaved Asparagus and Wagyu Tataki Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a large, pristine round bone china plate with a subtle, elegant pattern, resting on a polished white Carrara marble surface. The composition is organic and flowing, centered with abundant negative space. A delicate, airy mound of thinly shaved green asparagus ribbons, interwoven with crisp shaved crimson radish and vibrant baby rocket, forms the central element. A few thin, rosy-red slices of seared wagyu beef, exhibiting a perfect seared crust and a rare, glistening interior, are artfully placed atop or nestled within the vegetable mound, showcasing their exquisite marbling. A glossy, amber-hued yuzu-soy vinaigrette is precisely drizzled around the base and over parts of the salad, creating subtle pools and sheen. A light sprinkle of golden-brown toasted sesame seeds adds a textural contrast and subtle warmth. The overall impression is one of sophisticated simplicity and refined artistry, highlighting premium ingredients through precise knife work and thoughtful arrangement. The plate is viewed from a slightly elevated angle, with dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows, emphasizing the textures and layers against an ultra-minimalist background.

ingredients.name: wagyu beef tenderloin or sirloin, centre-cut

instructions: Using a vegetable peeler, shave asparagus spears lengthwise into thin ribbons. Discard tips and tough ends.
Season wagyu beef lightly with sea salt and white pepper.

Heat a heavy-bottomed pan or cast iron skillet over high heat until smoking. Sear wagyu beef for 30 seconds to 1 minute per side. Create a thin crust. Keep interior rare. Remove from heat. Rest beef for 5 minutes.
Using a very sharp knife, thinly slice the rested wagyu beef against the grain into 3-4 mm thick slices.
In a small bowl, whisk together yuzu juice, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, grated ginger, salt, and pepper.
Slowly drizzle in the extra virgin olive oil while whisking continuously until emulsified.
In a mixing bowl, gently toss the shaved asparagus ribbons, shaved radish, and baby rocket with a small amount of the yuzu-soy vinaigrette.
On each plate, create an artistic mound of the dressed vegetable mix.
Place 2-3 slices of wagyu tataki artfully on top or nestled within the vegetable mound.
Drizzle additional dressing around the salad. Sprinkle lightly with toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken & Cheese Buckwheat Blini
recipes.visual_description: A warm, inviting starter. Three or four golden-brown buckwheat blini are arranged slightly overlapping on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. Each blini is generously topped with a mound of creamy chicken and cheese mixture. The chicken pieces are small, uniform cubes, visible within the melted, slightly golden cheese sauce. The sauce has a rich, unctuous texture, clinging to the chicken and gently spreading over the blini. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped parsley adds a fresh contrast on top. The plate sits on a well-used, rustic wooden dining table, showing natural grain and slight imperfections. A simple, patterned cloth napkin is casually folded beside the plate. The lighting is warm and soft, suggestive of natural light filtering through a kitchen window or cozy overhead kitchen lighting. The background is minimally cluttered, showing hints of a home kitchen environment, perhaps a blur of a spice rack or a ceramic mug, reinforcing the homely atmosphere. A simple, sturdy fork and knife are placed beside the plate.

ingredients.name: Cheddar cheese (or similar meltable cheese), grated

instructions: Whisk egg and milk in a bowl.
Combine buckwheat flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder, and 2g salt in a separate bowl.
Gradually add wet ingredients to dry ingredients. Whisk until smooth batter forms. Let rest 10 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add a small amount of butter.
Pour 30ml of batter per blini. Cook 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer blini to a plate. Keep warm. Repeat with remaining batter.
Dice chicken breast into 1 cm cubes.
Chop onion into small cubes.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add diced chicken to the pan. Cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Season with salt and pepper.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in cream cheese or crème fraîche until melted and combined.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in grated cheese until melted and creamy.
Place 3-4 blini on each serving plate.
Spoon generous portion of creamy chicken and cheese topping onto each blini.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Chuck with Rosemary Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Braised Beef Chuck with Rosemary Roasted Potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Centrally, a generous portion of dark-brown, fork-tender braised beef chunks, approximately 5cm in size, are arranged. The beef is glistening with a rich, glossy, reduced sauce that pools slightly around the chunks. Beside the beef, golden-brown roasted potato wedges are neatly placed, showcasing their slightly crisp exterior and tender interior, with visible flecks of green rosemary adhering to their surfaces. A scattering of bright green, freshly chopped parsley leaves provides a vibrant contrast over the beef. The overall presentation is refined yet approachable, with ample negative space on the plate. The setting features a natural wooden table surface, a simple white linen napkin placed to the side, and standard polished silver flatware (fork and knife) complementing the dish. Natural, even lighting illuminates the food, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty bread for dipping into the sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Dredge lightly in flour.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the pot. Add chopped carrots, onion, and celery. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Add smashed garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until liquid reduces by half.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Cover pot tightly. Transfer to preheated oven. Braise 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Check internal temperature of beef, ensuring it is at least 75°C.
While beef braises, prepare potatoes. Toss potato wedges with 30 ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and 2 rosemary sprigs (leaves removed and chopped).
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast in the same oven as beef for 40-50 minutes, or until golden brown and tender. Flip halfway through.
Remove beef from oven. Discard bay leaves and herb sprigs. Skim any excess fat from the sauce, if desired. Stir in butter until melted. Adjust seasoning.
Serve braised beef chunks with a generous portion of sauce. Arrange roasted potato wedges alongside. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure beef reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Chorizo with Saffron Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single seared chicken thigh, skin-on and golden-brown, is the focal point, positioned centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Surrounding the chicken are vibrant saffron-tinted potato wedges, some showing slight crisp edges. Interspersed are bright red, slightly blistered cherry tomatoes and thick, smoky slices of chorizo. A light, glossy pan sauce, rich with paprika and tomato notes, pools subtly at the base of the chicken and potatoes. Freshly chopped green parsley is scattered generously over the dish, providing a contrasting color and fresh aroma. The arrangement is balanced and natural, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate, with standard flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the ingredients, creating an appetizing and approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful sauce.
Offer a small side of aioli for dipping.
Pair with a glass of Spanish red wine, such as Rioja or Tempranillo.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add chorizo slices to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes, turning once, until slightly crispy and fat is rendered. Remove chorizo and set aside, leaving rendered fat in the skillet.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, and diced red bell pepper to the skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Stir in smoked paprika and saffron threads. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the skillet with white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Cook for 2 minutes until liquid is reduced by half.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Add potato wedges to the skillet. Stir to coat.
Nestle the seared chicken thighs back into the skillet among the potatoes. Scatter cherry tomatoes and cooked chorizo around the chicken and potatoes.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender.
Remove from oven. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef Chili with Beans
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of beef and bean chili is served in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The chili presents a rich, dark reddish-brown hue, showcasing tender ground beef chunks, plump kidney beans, and softened tomato pieces suspended in a thick, savory sauce. A generous swirl of cool white sour cream sits centrally on top, lightly melting into the warmth below. It is generously sprinkled with bright green, finely chopped scallions and a scattering of golden shredded cheddar cheese, adding contrasting color and texture. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table, alongside a neatly folded cotton napkin and a sturdy spoon. A small side bowl contains golden, crisp tortilla chips, ready for dipping. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, highlighting the chili's inviting warmth and robust texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm cornbread or tortilla chips.
Offer shredded cheddar cheese, sour cream, and chopped green onions as toppings.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef. Brown thoroughly. Break up meat with a spoon.
Drain excess fat from the pot.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chili powder, cayenne pepper, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Stir well. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and beef stock. Stir to combine.
Add drained kidney beans.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Cover the pot and simmer for 60-90 minutes, stirring occasionally. Ensure beef reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove lid for the last 15 minutes if a thicker consistency is desired.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
notes: Adjust cayenne pepper quantity to your preferred spice level.
This chili can be made ahead and reheats well, often tasting even better the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Dijon Sauce
recipes.visual_description: Pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and succulent, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its perfectly seared crust. A rich, creamy Dijon sauce, glistening with a pale yellow hue, is elegantly spooned around the base of the chicken, creating a delicate pool. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh chives or parsley provides a vibrant green contrast and a fresh aroma. The dish is garnished simply, allowing the quality of the ingredients to shine. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, with a soft, blurred background maintaining focus on the food.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add minced shallot. Sauté 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer 2 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in chicken stock and Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 2-3 minutes. Do not boil vigorously.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Heat through 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Lamb Biryani
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of fragrant Lamb Biryani is centrally plated on a round white porcelain dish. The fluffy, long-grain basmati rice, exhibiting shades of saffron yellow and pristine white, is lightly mounded, revealing tender chunks of slow-cooked lamb underneath. The lamb pieces are rich, dark brown, and subtly sauced. Scattered over the top are crispy, golden-brown fried onions (birista) and vibrant green chopped cilantro and mint leaves. A lime wedge rests beside the biryani. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and a small katori bowl of cooling raita to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the steam rising gently, emphasizing the dish's warmth and aromatic appeal. The overall composition is clean, balanced, and inviting, showcasing the distinct layers and textures of this classic Indian dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cooling raita (yogurt dip with cucumber and mint).
Offer a small bowl of spicy salan (peanut-sesame-tamarind gravy) for added richness.
Provide sliced red onions and lime wedges for freshness.

ingredients.name: Saffron strands
ingredients.quantity: 1/4 teaspoon, soaked in 2 tablespoons warm milk

instructions: Wash basmati rice. Soak in cold water for 30 minutes. Drain well.

Marinate lamb chunks: Combine lamb with yogurt, ginger paste, garlic paste, 1 tablespoon biryani masala, turmeric, red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, and salt. Mix well. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Heat ghee or oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add thinly sliced onions. Fry until deep golden brown and crispy. Remove half the fried onions and set aside for garnish.
Add marinated lamb to the pot with remaining onions. Sear lamb chunks on all sides until lightly browned. This takes about 5-7 minutes.

Add chopped tomatoes and green chilies. Cook for 5 minutes until tomatoes soften. Add remaining 1 tablespoon biryani masala and garam masala. Stir well. Add 100 ml water. Cover and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until lamb is nearly tender. Stir occasionally.
While lamb cooks, bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add drained basmati rice. Cook until 70% done (al dente, with a slight bite). This takes about 5-7 minutes. Drain immediately.

Layer the biryani: Spread half of the par-cooked rice over the lamb curry in the pot. Sprinkle half of the chopped mint and cilantro. Add the remaining par-cooked rice. Top with the remaining mint and cilantro.
Pour the saffron milk evenly over the rice. Gently spread the reserved fried onions on top.
Cover the pot tightly with a lid, or seal with dough. Cook on low heat (dum cooking) for 20-25 minutes. This allows flavors to meld and rice to fully cook.
Turn off heat. Let biryani rest, covered, for 10 minutes before serving. Gently fluff with a fork.
notes: For best results, use good quality aged Basmati rice.
Ensure the pot is sealed tightly during dum cooking to trap steam and flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Broccoli Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy Chicken and Broccoli Risotto is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a pale, creamy yellow, flows naturally within the bowl. Diced, golden-seared chicken pieces (2 cm cubes) are visibly integrated, alongside vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets and flecks of deep amber caramelized onion. A small, elegant swirl of bright white lemon-herb mayonnaise rests on top, providing a contrasting color and texture. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley and a dusting of grated Parmesan. The setting is a modern bistro, with the bowl placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a fork and a crisp cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting. The background is subtly blurred, maintaining focus on the dish while suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pot; set aside.
Finely dice the onion. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion and cook over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Stir occasionally.
Mince garlic. Add minced garlic to the pot with onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes to toast rice kernels.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed.
Heat chicken broth in a separate saucepan; keep it simmering.
Begin adding hot broth to the rice, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 20-25 minutes.
While risotto cooks, steam or blanch broccoli florets until tender-crisp. Drain well.
When risotto is creamy and rice is al dente, stir in cooked chicken and broccoli florets.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in butter and half of the Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes until creamy and fluid. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Grate lemon zest. In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise with half of the chopped parsley and lemon zest. Mix well.
Serve risotto immediately in shallow bowls. Garnish each serving with a small dollop or swirl of lemon-herb mayonnaise, remaining Parmesan cheese, and a sprinkle of fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Peach Compote with Green Tea Cream
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in individual clear glass bowls or handcrafted ceramic bowls in earthy cream or beige tones, showcasing its natural beauty. Fermented peach cubes, approximately 1.5 cm, form the base, their natural color deepened by fermentation. A generous, smooth dollop of pale green tea cashew cream is elegantly placed beside the peaches, offering a soft color contrast.
